Sports.title: David Benavidez Targets Opetaia, Beterbiev, Usyk and Fury
Sports.content:
David Benavidez laid out a wish list featuring Jai Opetaia, Artur Beterbiev, Oleksandr Usyk and Tyson Fury, but his willingness to skip ahead to Usyk shows how quickly his cruiserweight plans could change.

“We got two great fights at cruiserweight before we get up there first,” Benavidez said to Inside Ring Show. “We got Jai Opetaia, then I think Beterbiev is going to come up to cruiserweight.” “If we can get a fight in with Usyk and Tyson Fury, then that’s something I’m willing to do.”

Benavidez appears to smell the money available at heavyweight. He describes his ambitions as a search for greatness, but Usyk and Fury also offer the possibility of enormous paydays. His interest extends beyond spending years building a cruiserweight reign.

The proposed sequence assumes plenty. Benavidez would need to secure those fights and win them to keep building toward the next one. Opetaia could derail that route through his southpaw combinations, movement, and experience at 200 pounds.

Beterbiev brings another threat, although Benavidez says there is interest from the other side.

“Beterbiev has definitely reached out to our team, and he’s been actively trying to make that fight,” he said.

That is more concrete than simply naming an opponent, but it still leaves the weight, timing, and agreement unresolved.

More revealing was Benavidez’s response to the possibility of Opetaia fighting Deontay Wilder. Rather than waiting, he suggested taking his business straight to heavyweight.

“If we can’t get that fight for Cinco de Mayo with Jai Opetaia, then we’ll do it with Usyk.”

That would be a substantial leap. Usyk’s movement and accuracy would test whether Benavidez could apply his pressure against an elite heavyweight. Fury’s size and reach would create a different set of difficulties.

Benavidez’s ambition is clear. What remains uncertain is how much of this list he can turn into reality. Naming four major opponents is easy compared with negotiating the fights and beating the men across from him.

Sports.title: Dmitry Bivol’s Vanishing Hunger Exposed
Sports.content:
Dmitry Bivol knows who he wants in the ring, but he is in no rush to lock down a contract. During an appearance on Inside the Ring, the champion singled out Artur Beterbiev, Canelo Alvarez, plus David Benavidez as his top targets. Still, he refused to pick one or name a date.

“This is Beterbiev, this is Canelo, and this is Benavidez,” Bivol said to Inside Ring Show. “This is three most big fights, I think, for me now.”

Bivol has the names ready. What is missing is any real urgency to get these bouts signed.

When asked about completing the Beterbiev trilogy by May, Bivol mentioned he would accept that timeline if all sides agreed. He pointed out that past talks hit roadblocks. That leaves fans with another vague target instead of a firm date. Waiting longer simply means Beterbiev gets older.

They split their previous two bouts. Unfinished business remains. Delaying the rubber match alters the physical test. While that does not prove Bivol wants to age his rival out, the advantage definitely leans his way.

Targeting Canelo makes pure financial sense. Bivol dominated their first clash, neutralizing the smaller boxer with ease. A return bout promises massive money against someone whose style he already mastered. Extra ring wear on Canelo only tilts the odds further in Bivol’s favor.

Benavidez offers a totally unique puzzle. Yet Bivol gave zero clues about when he wants that clash. He never clarified if he would jump to cruiserweight either.

Looking at other belts produced similar noncommittal answers. Bivol talked about how tough it feels jumping from 175 to 200 pounds, but skipped any mention of challenging Jai Opetaia.

His back surgery definitely plays a role in camp routines. He admits he must train smarter these days, which makes total sense. Even so, the core mystery lingers. Which major challenge does he actually want next?

Right now, Bivol is focusing entirely on Callum Smith. Past that date, his big plans stay strictly hypothetical. Something has changed with Bivol since his rematch with Beterbiev in February 2025. That twelfth round against Beterbiev took something out of him that a doctor cannot fix.

Bivol can talk all he wants about back rehabilitation and careful training camps, but the hesitation in his matchmaking tells the real story. When a fighter gets dragged into deep water, absorbs damage, and feels the fight slipping away beneath him with seconds left on the clock, it changes his wiring. Bivol survived that final barrage to collect the decision, but he walked away knowing exactly how violent that rivalry is. The appetite to jump straight back in with Beterbiev or any tough opponent has vanished.

Putting Canelo and Benavidez on a public wishlist is standard diversion. Canelo is a safe, massive payday against an opponent Bivol already solved without breaking a sweat. Benavidez is locked into cruiserweight campaigns, giving Bivol the perfect out to claim weight disparities prevent the bout. Meanwhile, Beterbiev is on the other side of forty, yet Bivol will not commit to a date to finish business.

Taking the Callum Smith fight while slow-walking the rubber match proves the point. Bivol went from an active technician hunting undisputed status to a cautious champion protecting his brand. When an elite boxer starts looking for reasons not to fight the very guys who tested his chin, the hunger is gone.

Sports.title: Max Kellerman Expects Terence Crawford To Fight Again
Sports.content:
Max Kellerman expects Terence Crawford to fight again, telling Ring Champs that Jaron “Boots” Ennis could eventually draw him out of retirement by giving him a challenge he cannot leave alone.

Kellerman puts the odds of Crawford never returning “close to zero.” His reasoning rests on Crawford’s competitive nature and the possibility that his desire to test himself returns as he gets older.

“I have zero inside information. This is not based on anything anyone’s telling me. This is my evaluation of human nature,” Kellerman said to Ring Champs.

Max believes the real test of Crawford’s retirement will come when he starts questioning how much time he has left. Being confident he can still beat everyone allows him to walk away without settling anything else. Feeling that ability beginning to slip could make another fight harder to pass up.

Ennis is the opponent Kellerman sees providing that temptation. He imagines Boots becoming the recognized champion at light middleweight, with talk about a Crawford fight bringing Bud’s competitive instincts back.

A Canelo Alvarez rematch would generate more business, Kellerman acknowledges, but he sees less sporting appeal because Crawford has already beaten him. Boots would offer an unanswered question, and delaying that fight could make the answer more difficult for Crawford.

“If you’ve been off for two years and you’re 40,” Kellerman said, “the worst kind of guy to have to fight is a twitchy, explosive offensive fighter.”

That is the danger in Max’s comeback scenario. Crawford’s timing and ability to read opponents have allowed him to take control of fights, but returning against a younger attacker after a long absence would ask more of him than returning against someone willing to give him room.

Kellerman would still pick Crawford until someone proves him wrong. Even so, he calls Ennis a “very dangerous” fight. His belief that Bud returns comes with a difficult consequence: the opponent who gives Crawford a reason to come back could become tougher to beat with every year he waits.

Sports.title: Jai Opetaia Explores Deontay Wilder Heavyweight Fight
Sports.content:
Jai Opetaia is looking at a jump to heavyweight against Deontay Wilder on the December 11 Tyson Fury against Anthony Joshua card in Cardiff, per Mike Coppinger at The Ring. It gives the cruiserweight king a marquee opponent immediately, plus an authentic test against heavyweight punch resistance.

The Ring notes talks are actively happening, though nothing is official yet. With the event streaming globally on Netflix, Opetaia lands a massive stage to introduce himself to a mainstream audience.

Wilder brings box office appeal. Fans tune in because that right hand can end any night instantly, even if Wilder loses every minute of every round beforehand. Watching an elite cruiserweight step up against an ex-champion sells easily, especially with Opetaia possessing the quickness to make things interesting.

Opetaia’s southpaw angles could leave Wilder searching for clean looks. The plan has to center on circling Wilder, firing quick bursts, then slipping out before the counter comes. Letting Wilder measure distance would be asking for trouble.

The main hazard for Opetaia is getting greedy after scoring clean hits. Lingering in range to admire his work opens the door for Wilder to unleash that signature right hand.

Beating Wilder gives Opetaia instant heavyweight credibility. It might not answer how he handles relentless physical bullies, but it delivers huge visibility overnight. Meanwhile, Wilder gets an opportunity to blast an ambitious cruiserweight daring to enter his territory.

It remains a significant introductory test. Opetaia can grab heavyweight credentials while putting his name in front of a global crowd. For Wilder, it offers an opening to knock out an intruder entering his weight class, where one flush right hand completely erases a clinic put on by Opetaia.

Wilder has looked like a shell of himself for years now. The punch volume has evaporated, the reflexes are shot, and the trigger hesitation is painful to watch. Against Joseph Parker and Zhilei Zhang, he barely threw anything, looked terrified of incoming traffic, and stood around waiting for an opening that never came because his timing is completely gone.

Against Opetaia, that hesitation is a sentence. Opetaia is fast, aggressive, fights out of a sharp southpaw stance, and doesn’t sit around waiting to be hit. He moves his head, changes direction constantly, and throws in vicious bursts before stepping out of the pocket. Wilder has always struggled with basic boxing fundamentals and awkward angles; an active, fleet-footed southpaw with elite ring IQ will have him spinning in circles, looking lost.

Sports.title: Jaime Munguia Faces Nikita Zon While Melikuziev Waits
Sports.content:
Jaime Munguia’s matchup with Nikita Zon raises the biggest question about the October 31 Riyadh undercard that Mike Coppinger describes as “stacked”: what happened to his ordered defense against Bektemir Melikuziev?

Coppinger hyped the Canelo Alvarez vs. Christian Mbilli undercard on X, pointing to Team Mexico’s combined 264-11 record against Team World’s 176-4. Those totals might impress casual fans, but adding up wins and losses tells readers little about whether the individual fights will be competitive.

The matchmaking heavily favors the Mexican side. The visiting opponents appear to have been picked to give the featured fighters wins, making “Mexico vs. The World” sound more competitive than the card looks on paper.

Munguia has been paired with a little-known opponent while his mandatory challenger waits. The WBA ordered Munguia to defend against Melikuziev on September 21, with negotiations running through October 21. The organization said his mandatory defense period had already expired on August 30.

The event’s official press release confirms Munguia will defend his WBA title against Nikita Zon (12-0-1) on October 31 in Riyadh. That makes the decision to bypass Melikuziev harder to explain. Zon is ranked ninth by the WBA, while Melikuziev is the mandatory challenger the organization has already ordered Munguia to face.

Zon is ranked ninth by the WBA, so he qualifies as a ranked contender. That does not explain why he should receive a title opportunity ahead of Melikuziev, who holds the mandatory position. Whether the WBA has approved Munguia–Zon as a voluntary title defense remains unconfirmed.

Reports that Munguia’s team offered Melikuziev step-aside money make the matchmaking harder to sell. Melikuziev reportedly rejected the offer and wants his title fight. Earlier reporting named Keiber Gonzalez as the proposed alternative opponent; now Zon appears on the announced card. The opponent has changed, but Melikuziev is still waiting.

The other listed bouts include Rafael Espinoza against Lorenzo Parra, Lindolfo Delgado against Arthur Biyarslanov, and David Picasso against Carl Martin. There are recognizable names on the Mexican side, but the lineup reads more like a series of fights designed to produce wins for the featured fighters than a collection of evenly matched contests.

Delgado–Biyarslanov offers some interest, and an underdog can always upset a promotion’s plans. Still, calling the entire undercard “stacked” oversells what is on paper.

Those combined records look good on a poster, but they don’t tell fans who these fighters have beaten. An unbeaten record built against weak opposition offers little proof that a challenger can compete with the opponent waiting for him in Riyadh.

Munguia vs. Nikita Zon exposes the real problem with this card. A fringe contender lands the Riyadh payday while Melikuziev, who has already earned his mandatory shot, gets pushed aside and told to keep waiting.

Sports.title: Bill Haney Targets November 28 for Shakur Stevenson
Sports.content:
Bill Haney wants Shakur Stevenson to fight Devin Haney on November 28 in Atlanta, putting a specific date and location behind a matchup that has spent months tangled in negotiations.

The date would leave Shakur just over seven weeks to prepare if the deal were completed immediately. Each additional week spent arguing would reduce that window, making the schedule another potential obstacle after the prolonged dispute over weight.

“There has been a challenge to their team to take the fight at 145 and a half and take it on the 28th of November in Atlanta,” Bill said to True Media podcast.

Bill later repeatedly identified 145 pounds as the final offer, consistent with the catchweight already discussed publicly. Asked again about the timing, he confirmed: “The offer is on the table for him to fight in November.”

Shakur looks more likely to reject Bill’s proposed date than agree to fight on November 28. An old-school fighter might accept the date and get to work after spending months pursuing the matchup. Shakur’s approach has been more cautious, with lengthy arguments over the conditions under which he will face the bigger Haney.

Accepting November 28 would also mean allowing the Haney camp to set the timetable. Shakur has negotiated as though he views himself as the A-side, or at least Devin’s equal. He could reject the date or push for a later fight rather than appear to be working to Bill’s schedule.

His current training situation is unknown, but any further delay would make November 28 harder to meet. The two camps could settle the weight dispute only to spend more time arguing over when to fight.

Bill said DAZN has made an offer, and he isn’t talking about anyone else for Devin. He wants Shakur next, but naming November 28 in Atlanta doesn’t mean Shakur will take it. Bill can push for that date all he wants. He still needs Shakur to agree, and after months of back-and-forth, that could take longer than he hopes.

Sports.title: Imam Khataev Targets Third Straight Win Against Padraig McCrory
Sports.content:
Imam Khataev seeks his third consecutive victory tonight against Padraig McCrory in a 10-round light heavyweight contest on DAZN at Capitole de Québec in Quebec City. The Olympic bronze medalist defends his NABF title on the Osleys Iglesias–Oliver Zaren undercard.

Khataev (12-1, 11 KOs) has stopped both opponents he has faced since his disputed split-decision loss to David Morrell in July 2025. Adam Deines lasted three rounds last December, while Mickael Diallo was stopped in the opening round in June. McCrory (20-2, 10 KOs) now gets the task of interrupting that run.

The Morrell performance remains the strongest evidence of what Khataev can do against higher-level opposition. He dropped the Cuban with a right hand in the fifth round and pushed him through a hard 10-round fight. Morrell got the decision, but Khataev’s promoter disputed the scoring and called for a rematch.

That leaves Khataev in a different position from a prospect whose potential rests entirely on knocking out overmatched opponents. He has already shown that his power and pressure can trouble a leading contender. The defeat added a loss to his record without settling how far he can go at 175 pounds.

McCrory offers another opportunity to build on that performance, although beating him would not answer every question left by the Morrell fight. Khataev needs opponents who can withstand his early attacks and force him to sustain his work deeper into a contest. His two quick stoppages have provided little opportunity to demonstrate that.

The temptation tonight will be to chase another early finish. Khataev’s power makes that a realistic outcome, but applying pressure without wasting punches would also serve him well when he returns to tougher opposition.

A third straight win would keep Khataev moving toward those fights. After the showing against Morrell, the next step should be another opponent capable of testing whether he can turn a competitive performance at that level into a victory.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury Wants Oleksandr Usyk Again After Joshua
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury wants a third fight with Oleksandr Usyk after Anthony Joshua, telling Rick Reno that his preferred finish would be victory in Cardiff followed by revenge at Madison Square Garden.

Usyk has already beaten him twice, but Fury remains interested in another attempt rather than a fresh opponent from the heavyweight division’s leading contenders.

“I want that rematch with him, that trilogy, because I know deep in my heart that I won those fights. And for whatever reason, he’s been given a decision over me,” Fury said to the Mr. Verzace podcast.

Fury described his ideal ending as beating Joshua in front of 80,000 in Cardiff, then going to Madison Square Garden to “get the revenge on the rabbit finally.” That is his preferred route, rather than an agreement for a third Usyk fight.

The appeal is understandable financially. Another meeting would likely produce an enormous payday, with two established names and a revenge story to sell. Fury could struggle to earn comparable money against Frank Sanchez, Filip Hrgovic or Moses Itauma.

There is also the knockout risk. Usyk isn’t a big puncher by heavyweight standards and is considerably smaller than Fury. He badly hurt Fury in their first meeting, so another fight would hardly be harmless, but Fury has twice completed 12 rounds against him.

Daniel Dubois, Fabio Wardley, Itauma, Hrgovic and Sanchez present different physical threats. They have the power to stop Fury, and facing one of them could mean accepting that danger for less money. Another points loss to Usyk would be easier to explain than getting knocked out by a new opponent.

Fury claiming robbery gives him the narrative hook to sell a trilogy. It lets him pitch a third bout as settling unfinished business rather than admitting he sits on two official losses to the same fighter.

Joshua remains the immediate hurdle in Cardiff. Fury must get past that domestic clash before any retirement tour holds weight. Overcoming Joshua opens the door to another massive payday against Usyk, all while keeping the division’s lethal young punchers safely locked on the outside.

Ghana News.title: Asos hackers took more personal details than first revealed, BBC finds
Ghana News.content:
Asos has told its customers that hackers are in possession of detailed profiles of potentially millions of the online store's users.

It issued the update after BBC News told the retailer it had been contacted by cyber criminals who said this week's breach went beyond the "basic contact details" Asos previously said might have been accessed.

Names, addresses, phone numbers, emails, customer numbers and dates of birth are now in the hands of criminals.

One victim told the BBC it was "very unsettling" that the hackers now know these things about her.

The criminals also have access to the searches customers have made on the website. Terms like "reclaimed vintage", "glamorous wide fit" and "Asos petite" are visible in the data.

Harriet has been using Asos since 2019 - another detail the hackers now know.

"What I find particularly worrying is the possibility that stolen data can be used as a tool for future attacks, meaning the impact of a breach could extend well beyond the initial incident," she said.

With the stolen information, scammers may be able to create convincing phishing attack emails or phone calls.

The risk to individuals is now higher, and customers are being warned about potential impersonation scams.

In its email to customers, Asos confirmed data profiles were taken but said no bank details or passwords were accessed.

"Please remain cautious of unexpected messages or calls claiming to be from Asos," it said.

"We will never ask you to share passwords, security codes or payment details through an unsolicited message or call."

The company did not respond to questions about the scale of the breach.

Customers saw this pop-up notification on Tuesday

The high-profile hack made global headlines on Tuesday when cybercriminals used Asos's own app to send a pop-up notification to potentially millions of people.

Later that day, the firm confirmed to shareholders via the London Stock Exchange that the pop-up was sent by an "unauthorised third party" and "basic personal information including name and contact details may have been accessed."

The company then sent an email to customers with similar wording.

On Wednesday evening, the cyber criminals responsible contacted the BBC, sharing a sample of the stolen data which showed the true extent of the hack.

The BBC held off publishing this article to allow Asos to contact its customers first.

'Impersonating a trusted contact'

Asos said it is still investigating the data breach and it would "contact customers directly where we believe additional information, support or action may be required".

The UK fashion site explained to customers that hackers gained access to an Asos employee account by "impersonating a trusted contact to obtain log in credentials".

With that login to an unnamed service, the hackers were able to download the customer data.

In the pop-up notification sent to customers by the hackers, they claimed they had "compromised the Snowflake instance".

Snowflake is a popular data storage and analysis company whose customers have been breached in the past due to unauthorised logins.

The cyber criminals, calling themselves Xuanyewen, claimed to the BBC that they used a platform built natively on top of Snowflake, called Simon AI, to gain access to the data.

Simon AI has been contacted for comment. Snowflake previously said its platform had not been breached.

Asos said customers are not being asked to take any action.

But cybersecurity experts have warned users to change passwords as a precaution and be on alert for suspicious activity.

"Passwords have not been stolen, so be highly suspicious of any unsolicited text or email asking you to change or share yours," said Trevor Dearing, Senior Director of Critical Infrastructure at Illumio.

"Expect scammers to mention the attack, use your personal details to seem genuine, and create urgency, such as threatening to lock your account within 24 hours."

Asos said its website and app are safe to use and "we know our customers trust us with their information".

"We take that responsibility seriously and have already taken additional steps to further strengthen security controls," it said.

Ghana News.title: Fort Hood shooter’s execution by firing squad will be livestreamed, Pentagon says
Ghana News.content:
US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth

The public will be able to watch the execution of a former US Army major by firing squad, US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth has said.

An official from the Defence Department told the BBC the execution of Nidal Hasan, who fatally shot 13 unarmed US soldiers at Fort Hood in 2009, would be livestreamed.

The Pentagon had announced earlier this week that it would execute Hasan in the first military execution in more than 60 years.

"We'll make sure that people are able to watch it, that it's public," Hegseth said on Thursday. "Because people need to understand that there's serious consequences for these types of things."

Hegseth said in an interview with conservative TV outlet Real America's Voice that Hasan is "gonna get a firing squad of soldiers. As it should be".

The BBC has contacted the White House for comment on whether President Donald Trump supports a livestreamed public execution.

The execution is scheduled to take place at Fort Hood in Texas on 3 December, the secretary of the US Army said on Tuesday. It will be the first military execution by firing squad since the end of World War Two.

The defence secretary had made the recommendation, and President Donald Trump approved it, Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell said on Monday.

Hasan, a US Army psychiatrist from Virginia, admitted in court that he was the gunman and apologised for "any mistakes". He said during his court-martial in 2013 that he believed he was protecting Muslims and the Taliban in Afghanistan.

The killings on 5 November 2009 were the deadliest ever non-combat attack on an American military base.

The shooting took place in a crowded medical building where deploying soldiers were awaiting check-ups and vaccines.

Ghana News.title: Chrysler Building to get its crown restored after being sold
Ghana News.content:
The skyscraper was briefly the world's tallest building

The Chrysler Building, one of the most distinctive high-rises in Manhattan's skyline, will undergo a major renovation as part of a multi-million-dollar sale deal.

The skyscraper, opened in New York nearly 100 years ago, will see its Art Deco crown polished and restored during a refurbishment that will also restore the building's 77-storey façade.

Developer Tishman Speyer has taken over the lease from the Cooper Union for the Advancement of Science and Art, a private college.

Tishman Speyer and its partners will invest $235m (£178m) in the project, as part of which it will upgrade the 61st floor, home to huge eagle gargoyles, and add an "upscale" lounge.

The developer plans to use most of the building, which is near Grand Central railway station, as office space. It is following what it calls a "prebuild approach" that will allow firms to move into their new premises quickly.

Tishman Speyer explained that the area "has one of the lowest office availability rates in Manhattan", adding: "Construction of new office supply in the neighbourhood has been virtually nonexistent for decades."

The renovation will include interior work, such as upgrades to the building's mechanical, elevator, electrical, and air-handling systems.

At 1,046ft (319m), the Chrysler Building was once the world's tallest building - before being usurped less than a year later by the nearby Empire State Building.

Financed by Walter Chrysler, the motor magnate, the skyscraper's construction began in 1928 and was completed two years later.

Architect William Van Alen modelled the eagle gargoyles on hood ornaments found on the 1929 Chrysler car.

Popping out for lunch: a worker eats a sandwich during construction of the Chrysler Building

The Cooper Union college, whose alumni include inventor Thomas Edison, has owned the land on which the Chrysler Building stands since 1902.

The land was bequeathed to it by the children of Peter Cooper, a manufacturer and industrialist who founded the college in 1859.

As part of the deal, Tishman Speyer will make ground lease payments to the Cooper Union, which the college wants to use to finance "a bold plan to restore full-tuition scholarships for all undergraduates".

Cooper Union's president Steven McLaughlin said: "The significance of this agreement is ultimately about what it makes possible for generations of Cooper Union students."

Ghana News.title: Infantino re-election boost as Concacaf chief will not stand
Ghana News.content:
Victor Montagliani was seen as a potential rival to Gianni Infantino's re-election bid

Gianni Infantino's chances of being re-elected as FIFA president appear to have received a major boost after potential rival Victor Montagliani confirmed he wants to remain head of Concacaf.

The Canadian, 61, was widely seen as a possible candidate after Infantino's failed plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors sparked a global backlash.

However, Montagliani never confirmed he wanted to challenge Infantino, and according to sources, he has now told colleagues that he will instead seek a final term as head of the confederation which governs North and Central America and the Caribbean.

As first reported by the Guardian, it means he will not stand against Infantino, 56, who has confirmed he will be seeking a fourth term in March's presidential election.

The rebellion against him, spearheaded by the European governing body UEFA, must now try to identify a unifying candidate by the deadline of 18 November.

Meanwhile, Aleksander Ceferin will stand for a fourth term as UEFA president.

Ceferin informed delegates of his decision at a meeting of all 55 national association chiefs in Berlin.

Uefa also reaffirmed its opposition to Infantino as it published a 14-point plan to reform world football's governing body.

Ceferin's move had been widely anticipated and reverses his insistence that he would not seek re-election, which the Slovenian outlined in February 2024.

At that point, Ceferin, who was initially elected in 2016, was embroiled in a row over UEFA's change to its statutes to allow him to serve a fourth term.

However, there had been a growing expectation that the 58-year-old would stand.

This has only become more likely since UEFA launched efforts to oust Infantino, who scrapped his sell-off plan following widespread opposition.

"I want to thank the national associations for their trust," Ceferin said.

"We have faced extraordinary challenges over the past years, and we have faced them as one team. There is still important work ahead, and I have therefore accepted their request.

"My ambition remains the same: to keep European football united, make our game stronger and leave UEFA ready for the next generation."

Ceferin has ruled out standing against Infantino himself but is committed to finding a candidate around which the game can unite in March's FIFA election.

UEFA sets out plans for FIFA reform

UEFA and 54 of its national associations, Azerbaijan being the exception, agreed on a clear direction for FIFA reform at the meeting.

As yet, no confirmed candidate has emerged to challenge Infantino in March.

Former Tottenham Hotspur and Switzerland defender Ramon Vega says he intends to stand, but it is unclear whether he can even garner the five letters of support required to get on the ballot paper.

"Institutional reform will not, on its own, be enough," UEFA said.

"FIFA also needs new leadership: a respected and unifying figure, deeply rooted in football, with the vision and experience to lead, the ability to command confidence across regions and an unequivocal commitment to development, reform, integrity and independence."

Much of UEFA's plan centres around institutional governance and removes some of the direct powers of the president, which led to the creation of the FIFA Forward Enterprise proposal behind closed doors.

It also said that presidential or executive interference must be removed from oversight bodies which cover ethics and disciplinary matters.

UEFA added that no FIFA resources should be used for personal or electoral interests, and that at least $10m (£7.5m) of additional funding should be made available to each of the 211 member associations.

Ghana News.title: Everton’s Sherif fined for breaching betting rules
Ghana News.content:
Martin Sherif joined Everton's youth set up in 2019

Everton forward Martin Sherif has been fined £5,000 by the Football Association for breaching its betting rules over a 15-month period.

The 20-year-old admitted having caused, permitted or enabled 61 bets on games between 20 November 2024 and 12 February 2026.

In his defence, Sherif said he did not place any of the bets himself but admitted they came from accounts in his name, which he funded.

An independent regulatory commission said Sherif had shown "genuine remorse".

The striker, who was born in Liberia and is a Netherlands youth international, joined Everton's youth set-up in 2019 and began training with the first team in early 2025.

In February, he joined Port Vale on loan for the remainder of the season, scoring twice in 17 League One appearances as the club was relegated.

Ghana News.title: Suspended fine for Xhaka over Covid-19 certificate
Ghana News.content:
Sunderland and Switzerland captain Granit Xhaka says he has received a suspended fine of 150,000 Swiss francs (£136,000) for obtaining a forged Covid-19 vaccination certificate.

The 34-year-old, who is alleged to have obtained the certificate in 2022, when it was required in Switzerland for travel abroad, says the fine is suspended for two years, provided he does not commit any further offences, and that he has already paid the court costs.

"A few weeks ago, I spoke personally here and said that I would take responsibility for my decision. I stand by that," the midfielder wrote in German on Instagram.

"I was sentenced by summary judgment for obtaining a false certification to a suspended fine of 50 daily rates of CHF 3,000 [£2,726] each.

"I accept the decision and take responsibility for my actions. Thank you for the many messages of support over the past few weeks. They mean a lot to me."

Xhaka was playing for Arsenal in 2022 and posted a statement on social media on 21 September saying he had a "mistrust" towards the vaccine and that he had been "influenced by worries and uncertainty".

He is Switzerland's record appearance holder with 152 caps and, following his initial statement, withdrew from his country's camp for their Nations League matches against Scotland, North Macedonia and Slovenia in the international break that has just concluded.

The Swiss office of public health had confirmed that while there was never a general legal requirement to obtain or hold such a certificate, it was needed for access to various activities, venues and travel, meaning that participation was restricted for anyone who did not possess one.

These measures in Switzerland were in place until the spring of 2022. After that point, Covid-19 certificates continued to be issued, primarily to enable members of the public to meet entry requirements when travelling abroad.

Xhaka captained Switzerland at the World Cup earlier this year, where they were knocked out in the quarter-finals by eventual runners-up Argentina.

He is expected to return to action when Sunderland host Brighton on Saturday (15:00 BST).

Black Cats boss Regis le Bris said: "No comment on external topics but [from] what I've seen during the international break, he has trained really well. It's positive. He's in a good place football-wise and for me that is the most important."

Ghana News.title: Businessman dragged to court over GH¢480,000 fraud
Ghana News.content:
A 44-year-old businessman has appeared before an Accra Circuit Court on charges of allegedly defrauding a businesswoman of GH¢480,000.

Anthony Appiah, charged with defrauding by false pretences, pleaded not guilty.

The court admitted him to bail in the sum of GH¢500,000 with two sureties, one of whom must be a public servant earning not less than GH¢4,000.

Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP) Emmanuel Nyamekye led the prosecution.

The prosecution said the complainant, whose name was withheld, was a businesswoman who resided in Accra, as did Appiah.

It said in May 2025, Appiah, who had known the complainant for some time, visited her home and told her that he had secured a distribution contract with BEL-AQUA Company.

He allegedly said he needed $50,000 to execute the contract and appealed to the complainant for financial assistance, promising to refund the money within two weeks.

The complainant subsequently gave Appiah GH¢480,000.

However, after the two-week period elapsed, Appiah failed to refund the money.

The prosecution said the complainant contacted BEL-AQUA Company to verify the contract and was informed that Appiah had no such contract with the company.

All efforts to recover the money proved unsuccessful, prompting the complainant to petition the Police to investigate.

Appiah was subsequently arrested, and investigations established that BEL-AQUA Company had neither awarded him any contract nor engaged him in any capacity.

Ghana News.title: Pregnant woman and husband found dead in a room at Anloga-Kportorgboe
Ghana News.content:
A 35-year-old man and his pregnant wife have been found dead in their room at Kportorgboe, a suburb of Anloga in the Volta Region.

The incident has left residents in shock and struggling to comprehend.

Mr Edwin Kwasi Vedzi, the Assembly Member of Anloga Kportorgbe Electoral Area, disclosed the information to the Ghana News Agency and identified the deceased as Daniel Agbenyegah, a mason, and his wife, Patience Awumee.

Mr Vedzi said Ms Awumee, who previously sold eggs, would be between 29 and 30 years old and carrying a pregnancy of about seven months.

“Preliminary information indicates that the man allegedly killed his wife with a knife before taking his own life, and we are waiting for the police to confirm this account, since the circumstances remain unverified. The throats of both the deceased have been slashed,” he said.

He explained that further information gathered indicated that the couple had travelled on Sunday to visit the woman’s parents and returned on Monday at about 1100 hours, while the incident was said to have occurred roughly half an hour after their return.

He also told the GNA that the couple lived in the house of the husband’s grandfather, along with other relatives.

However, the neighbours said they were not on speaking terms with the occupants of the house and that nobody had noticed any altercation.

Mr Vedzi said what led to the tragedy was unknown, as there was no quarrel between the couple that residents and neighbours were aware of.

The Police later removed the bodies and deposited them at the Keta Municipal Hospital Morgue for further examination and autopsy.

The Assemblyman urged residents to remain calm and to cooperate with the police in their investigations to establish the cause of the deaths.

The deaths have left the Kportorgbe community in shock, with condolences going out to the bereaved families and loved ones as the police was expected to release details of their findings once investigations and the autopsy were completed.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Hegseth says firing squad execution of Fort Hood shooter will be ‘public’
World.content:
An official at the Pentagon told Al Jazeera that former US Army Major Nidal Hassan’s execution would be ‘livestreamed’.

Share Hegseth says firing squad execution of Fort Hood shooter will be ‘public’ on social media

United States Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has said the execution of a former US Army psychiatrist who killed 13 people at the Fort Hood military base in Texas will be publicly available to watch.

In an interview with the media outlet Real America’s Voice on Thursday, Hegseth was asked about President Donald Trump’s recent order to use a firing squad to execute Nidal Hasan, who was convicted of the 2009 shooting.

The secretary said he approved of the decision, calling it a “no-brainer”.

“We’ll make sure that people are able to watch it, that it’s public,” Hegseth told interviewer Jack Posobiec. “Because people need to understand that there’s serious consequences for these types of things.”

Hegseth added that the execution would take place at Fort Hood on December 3 at 1pm US Central Time (19:00 GMT), the same time that the 2009 shooting took place.

Hasan was sentenced to death in August 2013 after a military jury found him guilty of 45 counts of premeditated murder and attempted murder for the shooting.

The former Army major walked into an army processing centre on the Texas base, shouted “Allahu akbar” (God is greatest) and opened fire on fellow military members waiting to get medical attention.

Hasan’s execution required approval from Hegseth and Trump, who authorised the use of the firing squad on Monday.

An official with the Defense Department told Al Jazeera that Hasan’s execution would be “livestreamed”, adding that more details would come soon.

It is not clear from Hegseth’s remarks whether troops, spectators or US military officials would be present in person for the execution. US Army regulation states that at least two media outlets should be selected as witnesses.



No state or federal execution has ever been televised in the US. The last public execution in the country took place more than 90 years ago in Owensboro, Kentucky, on August 14, 1936.

The last time a US military execution was conducted by firing squad was in 1945, for desertion during World War II.

When asked to comment on Hegseth’s remarks – and whether Trump would view the execution – the White House referred Al Jazeera to the Pentagon.

The Trump administration announced it would add death by firing squad as an acceptable method for federal executions in April, along with gas asphyxiation and electrocution.

World.title: Man City charges: Mourinho jokes Premier League case will outlast him
World.content:
Jose Mourinho, one of most outspoken against Man City spending when United manager, jibes EPL appeal to outlast him.

Share Real Madrid’s Mourinho digs at Man City appeal saying it will outlast him on social media

Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho joked that he may not live to see the end of Manchester City’s legal battle with the Premier League after the club appealed against a ruling that found it guilty of serious financial rule breaches.

An independent commission found City guilty of all charges relating to breaches of Premier League financial regulations between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons, as well as three of four charges relating to failures to cooperate with the investigation. City have denied wrongdoing and lodged an appeal.

The Premier League said that City used “sham” commercial agreements to inflate revenue and understate costs by more than 900 million pounds ($1.19bn) over nearly a decade, resulting in inaccurate financial reporting and breaches of spending rules.

Mourinho managed Manchester United from 2016 to 2018 and led them to a second-placed Premier League finish behind Pep Guardiola’s City in 2017-18.

“I would rather laugh about it,” Mourinho said when asked about the case in an interview with Italy’s Corriere dello Sport.

“I think we will eventually get an ending, but we are both in our 60s, and we’ll need to be lucky enough to still be around when the final verdict arrives.

“There will be a verdict, then appeals, then more appeals.”

Mourinho has long maintained that one of his greatest achievements in football management was finishing second behind Guardiola’s side, given their spending power at the time.

The Portuguese manager, now 63, said in 2024 that he had not given up on being awarded a winner’s medal for the 2018 season.



“I think we still have a chance to win that league because maybe they punish Man City with points and maybe we win that league,” he quipped at a press conference ahead of a Europa League match against United with his then-club, Fenerbahce.

“Then they have to pay me the bonus and give me the medal.”

The appeal process will be conducted in private, and it remains unclear whether any sanctions would be imposed before it is heard, or whether any punishment would take effect immediately.

City, seeking a sixth successive league win, are top of the Premier League with 15 points from five matches and travel to Liverpool on Sunday.

Holders Arsenal entertain Leeds on Saturday, while United host Tottenham later the same day.

Mourinho’s Real Madrid trail fierce rivals and La Liga leaders Barcelona by six points, with five wins and two defeats from their seven league matches this season.

Both Barca and Real are in action on Saturday, with Getafe and Villarreal visiting, respectively.

World.title: Israel kills or wounds Palestinian every 90 minutes in Gaza since ceasefire
World.content:
Share Israel kills or wounds Palestinian every 90 minutes in Gaza since ceasefire on social media

Israeli attacks have killed or wounded a Palestinian in Gaza every 90 minutes on average since the ceasefire was announced in October last year, the aid group Islamic Relief says.

Islamic Relief, a United Kingdom-based charity, said on Thursday that at least 1,454 Palestinians were killed and more than 5,000 wounded over the year. At least 320 of those killed were children, close to one a day.

Gaza’s Health Ministry reported that 1,471 Palestinians have been killed and 5,189 wounded since the ceasefire, including four killed and 28 wounded in the past 24 hours.

Israel has killed at least 74,254 people since October 2023, the ministry added.

On Thursday, Israeli forces killed a Palestinian southeast of Deir el-Balah, in central Gaza, and an Israeli air strike on a house in central Khan Younis wounded several people, the Palestinian news agency Wafa reported.

In the occupied West Bank, a 13-year-old boy was shot in the foot during an Israeli raid on Yamoun, west of Jenin, the Palestinian Red Crescent said.

Islamic Relief said Israel has used the so-called Yellow Line, which marks the area under Israeli military control, to push Palestinians out of 65 percent of Gaza, crowding its nearly 2.1 million people into the remaining 35 percent.

According to the report, an Islamic Relief aid worker in Gaza whose name is withheld for their safety said: “There is no ceasefire in reality. They target displacement camps and crowded areas, so there is still a lot of fear.”

Israel continues to block shelter materials, fuel and medical supplies, the group said.



About 82 percent of Gaza’s structures are damaged or destroyed, more than half of health services have shut down and more than 20,000 severely ill patients are denied permission to leave for treatment.

The charity urged world leaders to increase pressure to protect civilians and uphold international law.

“A ceasefire in name only cannot be an excuse for international inaction,” it said.

World.title: Putin pledges Russia’s support to end US-led war on Iran
World.content:
The Russian and Iranian presidents met in Turkmenistan ahead of regional summit.

Russian President Vladimir Putin has told Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian that Russia will “do everything” to help end the United States-led war on Iran, Russian news agencies reported.

The two leaders met in Turkmenistan on Thursday ahead of the summit of the Commonwealth of Independent States, a group of former Soviet nations.

“You know our position. On our part, we are ready to do everything we can to help you resolve this situation,” Interfax news agency said Putin told Pezeshkian.

“We know that Iran is making real efforts to end the conflict, which broke out through no fault of its own, no fault of Iran’s,” Putin said, according to Russian media.

Putin also noted what he called a “positive evolution” in Iran-Russia relations.

In a call on Wednesday, Putin told Pezeshkian that Moscow is prepared to mediate efforts to end the war in the Middle East, Iran’s IRNA news agency reported.

Putin and Pezeshkian also met on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Kyrgyzstan last month.

Strategic partnership

The two countries, which are under heavy Western sanctions, have reinforced diplomatic and military ties.

Last year, Moscow and Tehran signed a “comprehensive strategic partnership treaty” that covers areas from trade and military cooperation to science, culture and education.

Ukraine and Western countries have accused Iran of supplying Russia with Shahed drones and short-range missiles for use in the Ukraine war. Russia has also been accused of supplying data to Iran for its attacks on US targets in the Middle East.



The meeting came as Iran-US talks stand at an apparent impasse.

US President Donald Trump said on Thursday that the US will not launch an attack on Iran before the November 3 US midterm congressional elections, saying the two countries are ‌‌holding “productive” talks about ending the ongoing war.

Diplomatic efforts to resolve Russia’s offensive in Ukraine also appear deadlocked, even as both sides intensify attacks.

World.title: French giants Bordeaux relegated to sixth tier for financial irregularities
World.content:
Six-time French champions Bordeaux, the club where Zinedine Zidane made his name, to play in sixth tier after sanctions.

Share French giants Bordeaux relegated to sixth tier for financial irregularities on social media

Six-time French champions Bordeaux, sanctioned in the summer for financial irregularities, will play in the sixth tier of French football this season, the Nouvelle-Aquitaine league confirmed on Thursday.

Bordeaux were sanctioned for failing to provide the roughly 10 million euros ($11.6m) needed for the 2025-26 and 2026-27 financial years and to meet debt payments.

Once one of France’s leading football clubs and the team where the country’s new head coach, Zinedine Zidane, made his name, Bordeaux was sold last month for a symbolic one euro to US-based investment group Park Bench, which agreed to take on the remaining debt.

Two days after appearing before the Nouvelle-Aquitaine league oversight commission, which approved its recovery budget and issued “a positive opinion on their possible participation in Regional 1”, the club was unanimously approved to play in the top regional tier.

“Rebuilding can now begin,” said Dominique Delport, the new president chosen by Park Bench, speaking to the AFP news agency.

The new owners are due in commercial court on October 20 to ratify the new continuation plan, which now runs over 12 years, with the debt halved from 26 million to 13 million euros.

The team is largely amateur, though the club can field five players on professional contracts, one of whom will be former Ligue 1 striker Baptiste Guillaume.

The club has produced many big names of French football, including academy products Bixente Lizarazu and Christophe Dugarry, who both played alongside Zidane in the 1998 World Cup-winning team.



More than a decade earlier, Alain Giresse and Jean Tigana were part of a celebrated France midfield that won the 1984 European Championship.

However, they were relegated to Ligue 2 in 2022 and then placed under judicial restructuring in 2024, which caused them to relinquish their professional status and their highly rated academy.

World.title: Four astronauts return to earth after an eight-month space mission
World.content:
Four astronauts return to earth after an eight-month space mission

NewsFeed Four astronauts return to earth after an eight-month space mission

Four astronauts returned to Earth on Thursday from an eight-month mission to the International Space Station. The crew completed a parachute-assisted splashdown in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of California.

World.title: What Man City charges anger Liverpool before Premier League game?
World.content:
Clubs are reportedly exploring claims after Man City verdict – one of those, Liverpool, are first opponent in fallout.

Manchester City are preparing for their first football match since receiving a guilty verdict for multiple breaches of Premier League financial rules and – of course – their opponent on Sunday is one of the clubs that hold grievances over their losses during the seasons in question.

Liverpool’s Anfield crowd is expected to deliver an angry reception for the Premier League clash, and City manager Enzo Maresca and his players must prepare for the backlash to continue throughout the game itself.

City have protested their innocence and have appealed the verdict that went against them on more than 100 charges of financial wrongdoing.

Still, the scandal remains the biggest in the history of club football’s richest, most competitive and most popular league, and the backlash from the stands is likely to linger long after any appeal outcome or potential punishments are finalised.

The current crop of players and staff are quite simply going to have to face the music for charges that stretch from 2009 to 2018.

The fact that their opening match after the international window, when the guilty verdict was delivered, is at Anfield is something that a scriptwriter may even pause to think is outlandish.

“If they want an understanding of how angry the game ⁠is going to be, then Anfield will tell them like you would never believe,” former Manchester United captain and England defender Gary Neville declared recently on The Overlap podcast.

“I suspect there may be banners, there will certainly be chanting. There will be a reception like you have never seen for them at Anfield… it will be a brutal day.”

Why are Liverpool set to give Man City an angry reception?

Of all the clubs that finished second best to City since the Abu Dhabi buyout, Liverpool will argue that they have been among the hardest hit.



There is a growing feeling that any titles that City are stripped of should be awarded to their nearest rivals, or defeated finalists, during the period investigated.

For Liverpool, however, their two closest calls with City came after 2018.

Under former coach Jurgen Klopp, Liverpool won the Premier League in 2020, but the team also finished second to Pep Guardiola’s City by one point in the 2018-19 and 2021-22 seasons.

Both were memorable title races that raised the bar in terms of points earned and the standard of football played.

Neither will see Liverpool retrospectively awarded the title if the Premier League does indeed choose to go down that path regarding honours won in the seasons that were under investigation.

Liverpool’s fans will assert, and most likely vociferously argue on Sunday, that what helped City reach that level was nearly a decade of rule-breaking, as the independent panel has found.

Liverpool do, however, have a claim to at least one title in the period in question.

The Reds, under Brendan Rodgers, finished runners-up by two points to City in 2013-2014 – Steven Gerrard’s infamous slip in a match against Chelsea the moment etched on everyone’s memory from that campaign.

It left the Anfield faithful continuing their wait for a first top-flight title since 1990.

Only weeks earlier, Gerrard was the star of the show as Liverpool beat City 3-2 to seemingly put one hand on the elusive title.

Any retrospective award of titles could see club legend Gerrard finally hold a Premier League winner’s medal.

Do any of Man City’s current setup remain from the period of the charges?

Aside from Phil Foden, who is suspended for the match, no current member of City’s squad even played for the club from 2009-2018.

Enzo Maresca, who was a youth-team coach for City in 2020-21 and was assistant to Guardiola in 2022-2023, took over as City’s first-team manager only in June.

Still, they will be the ones bearing the brunt of the widespread discontent from fan bases up and down the country in the coming months.

What will be intriguing is who from City’s ownership or board attends the Liverpool game.

How much will the matter weigh on the players under the most intense pressure? And what will be the reaction of City’s match-going supporters, with the future of their club so uncertain – the potential sanctions include a huge points deduction, even expulsion from the Premier League – and the violations of its ownership clear for all to see in the commission’s verdict?

City lead the league with five wins from five games – all of which were played when the club was being accused of those financial breaches.



Now the guilty verdict has arrived, it’s time to see the impact on the team – and the reaction of its rivals.

World.title: Police use tear gas and water cannons on student protestors in Paris
World.content:
Police use tear gas and water cannons on student protestors in Paris

NewsFeed Police use tear gas and water cannons on student protestors in Paris

Police fired tear gas and water cannons as demonstrators gathered in Paris to demand more funding, teachers, and better conditions in schools. The movement has entered its third week, with police tactics under scrutiny after several teenagers were seriously injured.

World.title: Suspect linked to Monaco bomb attack on millionaire breaks silence to BBC
World.content:
A former Ukrainian security services officer linked to a bomb attack in Monaco in June that targeted a multi-millionaire says he believed it was ordered by senior members of HUR, Ukraine's military intelligence agency.

In an exclusive interview with the BBC from prison in Kyiv, facilitated by his lawyer, Vitalii Zhykovych has given his own account of the attempted assassination for the first time.

Ukrainian-born businessman Vadym Yermolayev and his 13-year-old son were badly hurt in the blast and his partner suffered catastrophic injuries. Yermolayev later described their survival as "nothing short of a miracle".

Zhykovych describes himself as a "freelancer" for Ukraine's SBU security service and says Anastasia Berezovska, the woman caught on camera planting the bomb in Monaco, was his "agent".

A week after the bombing, Berezovska's body was discovered in the woods west of Kyiv with gunshot wounds to the head.

But Zhykovych insists he did not send her to kill, and nor did he kill her.

He was arrested and accused of her murder together with an active-duty intelligence officer from HUR called Vladyslav Reut.

Reut initially confessed to investigators, and led them to the shallow grave. But days later in court, he changed his testimony to blame Zhykovych.

World.title: Fort Hood attacker's execution by firing squad will be livestreamed, Pentagon says
World.content:
There is no modern-era precedent for having a public execution, said John Mills, a lawyer who works with inmates sentenced to death.

"It looks to me designed to be a grotesque spectacle," he said. "It's an unprecedented decision in the modern era, and so it is on uncertain legal terrain," he added.

A military execution requires approval from the US president, according to military law. It also requires appellate review, where a higher court inspects the decision, and a final judgment on its legality to move forward.

The appellate process for Hasan is not over, Mills said, and he is likely to seek review of his conviction and sentence in federal court, which would likely stay the execution.

As such, Mills said that he would be surprised if the execution happened.

"Seeking to make it livestreamed, a firing squad execution, is little more than attention-seeking by the Trump administration and is unlikely to occur, much less deliver any semblance of justice," he added.

Certain states require some form of public viewing of executions. Many states require journalists to be present, and the person due to be executed can invite people. Others also allow ordinary citizens to volunteer as witnesses.

But "there hasn't ever been a livestreamed execution," says Deborah Denno, a law professor at Fordham University, who has studied US execution methods.

A livestreamed execution would "force a level of transparency that we have probably never seen before in this country", she says.

"More than half of the country wants the death penalty - even though that's on the decline - an argument could be made that 'if you want the death penalty, then we are going to show you how it's conducted in this country'. And people would have to realise exactly what's happening in a way that many people ignore."

Denno says there are important considerations for a livestream such as whether it would be age-redistricted and whether it would contravene the policies of the online platform that hosts the viewing.

It is unclear where the livestream will be available. Most major social media platforms have rules that prohibit or restrict livestreaming explicit content.

World.title: Russian strike on buses kills at least 30, say officials, as deadly attacks on Ukraine surge
World.content:
At least 30 people have been killed in a Russian glide bomb attack on two civilian buses in the eastern front line city of Kramatorsk, rescue officials say.

Authorities said three people were also killed in the village of Bilenke, part of the Kramatorsk community.

Another 18 people were wounded, said Donetsk regional head Vadym Filashkin, accusing Russia of targeting buses carrying passengers to kill as many civilians as possible.
