Kramatorsk and neighbouring Slovyansk are part of a so-called fortress belt that Moscow is trying to seize as part of Russian President Vladimir Putin's claim to the entire Ukrainian industrial region of Donbas.

Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky said: "This strike will not go without our response."

In a post on Telegram, he said: "Russia is trying to destroy all life in Donbas, and the world needs to react to this. React harshly - exactly as the Russians deserve for all the deaths they have caused."

Images posted by local prosecutors showed the burning metal shell of the bus along with debris and some of the victims on the road.

Moscow is yet to comment on the latest attack. It follows a dramatic surge in Russian attacks across Ukraine and a heavy increase in civilian casualties.

According to the UN, Ukraine saw more civilians killed by August this year than were killed in all of 2025.

In one single attack that destroyed a five-storey block of flats in Pryluky east of Kyiv early on Wednesday, 22 people were killed, including five children. Three of the children were only one year old.

UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband, who together with Zelensky visited the site of the Russian strike in Pryluky, said the attack showed Putin's "evil intent and evil strategy".

He announced "more sanctions on Russia, on the war machine of Putin, on the shadow fleet, on the oil companies, on the crypto, on the financing of the war" and told Zelensky the UK would stand with Ukraine "as long as it takes for you to prevail in this conflict".

World.title: Christa Pike now walking after failed US execution, lawyer tells BBC
World.content:
Christa Pike is "up and walking" though mentally "foggy" while in hospital after last week's botched attempt to execute her in the US state of Tennessee, her legal team says.

Pike, 50, who was sentenced to death after murdering Colleen Slemmer with her then-boyfriend in 1995, survived two lethal injections on 30 September. Experts described it as unprecedented.

Speaking late on Wednesday to BBC Radio 4's Today programme, lawyer Stephen Ferrell said he had not spoken to Pike directly but had learned her arms were swollen and barely functioning as she took her first steps around her hospital room.

A court has ordered state officials to preserve all evidence related to the failed execution.

That evidence could lay the groundwork for a future lawsuit against the state.

The Pike case is now in uncharted territory, as Pike is believed to be the only person to have survived an execution attempt by lethal injection.

The failed execution was branded a "mess" by the mother of Slemmer, who was among those pushing for Pike to be put to death.

Pike's boyfriend at the time of Slemmer's gruesome murder, Tadaryl Shipp, was spared the death penalty because he was not legally an adult when the crime was committed. He remains in prison.

Pike was 18 and Shipp was 17 when they beat, tortured and killed 19-year-old Slemmer, whom they had met at a job training camp for low-income young people.

World.title: Adidas sues Australian label White Fox over four stripes design
World.content:
Adidas is suing Australian label White Fox for selling and advertising clothes with a four-striped design, arguing it is "deceptively similar" to the German brand's distinct logo.

The sportswear giant said it had repeatedly asked White Fox to stop selling and promoting the clothes since March, but the Sydney-based company refused.

The fast-fashion online retailer is popular with teenagers and young adults in Australia, the UK and the US, and has relied on billboards, bus advertising and influencers - often university-aged - to grow its profile.

The Australian law firms representing Adidas and White Fox both declined to comment on the case, the first hearing due to begin on Friday.

In Federal Court documents, Adidas states that its three-striped design has a "substantial and valuable reputation" in Australia, where it has been trademarked since 1957.

The company says since at least March, White Fox has been selling and advertising clothes with four parallel stripes of equal width, which it claims is an infringement of Adidas's trademark.

White Fox's designs are "substantially identical with or otherwise deceptively similar" to Adidas, the company claims.

It also argues that White Fox's s for its four-striped clothes and White Fox-branded socks feature people wearing "genuine" Adidas items.

This might lead Australians to think Adidas is associated with White Fox and has approved of the design, the documents claim.

The company says White Fox is "taking advantage" of Adidas's reputation, "drawing an association in the minds of consumers" of the two brands, or at least "sailing close to the wind".

Adidas, which reported â¬24.8 billion (Â£21bn; $28bn) in revenue in 2025, is also seeking damages, saying White Fox must pay them the profit from the products plus interest and costs.

World.title: Protesters blame 'vulture funds' for Spain's housing crisis
World.content:
Pierina Nicuray, a 21-year-old university graduate, has spent a week camped out in Madrid's Puerta del Sol square.

Like many of the hundreds of others who have pitched their tents here to protest at Spain's housing crisis, she has no doubts when it comes to diagnosing the cause.

"It's the same problem as always," she says. "A lack of homes."

She adds: "Landlords are taking advantage of the situation to raise rentals, and then there's also Airbnb."

Jorge Moreno, a 19-year-old film-dubbing student who has also been living in a tent here in central Madrid for the last few days, agrees.

"There are so many homes standing empty because they have been bought by vulture funds and investment funds which hike up the rent of people living in properties until they get rid of them," says Jorge, who lives with his mother and fears it will be a long time before he can afford a home of his own.

"They've been making a business of housing for a long time," he adds. "But it's an abusive business which stops Spaniards from being able to live in a decent home."

His and Pierina's diagnoses are frequently voiced by fellow protesters, ordinary Spaniards and even the Spanish government.

On presenting a recent package of emergency measures to tackle the housing problem, Socialist Prime Minister Pedro SÃ¡nchez said he was legislating "against those who consider housing just another object on the market with which to speculate".

Those reforms were rejected by Congress, prompting SÃ¡nchez to call a snap election next month.

Nicuray and Moreno can point to the single case that sparked the current Spanish housing protest movement as proof that profit-driven practices are at the heart of the crisis: the 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal was evicted from her home after the investment firm that had bought it tried to persuade her to leave, then sharply increased her rent, which she was unable to pay.

Although the social backlash that followed caused the company to invite Abascal to return to her old home, she never did, dying in hospital on Wednesday.

World.title: 'Bold and inventive' Canadian poet Anne Carson wins Nobel Literature Prize
World.content:
Canadian poet, essayist and translator Anne Carson has been awarded this year's Nobel Prize in Literature.

Carson, 76, is celebrated for works that often cross the boundaries between poetry, fiction and scholarship.

The Nobel Prize committee said they had selected her "for her bold and inventive oeuvre that, in playful dialogue with the classical tradition, has created new forms for contemporary literature".

Carson responded by joking that the judges were "crazy" for honouring her. "I think they're all crazy... Well, you know, it's crazy," she told public broadcaster RUV in Iceland, where she is currently staying.

The Nobel Prize is awarded for a lifetime's body of work and is regarded as the most prestigious award in global literature, with the winner receiving 12 million Swedish kronor (Â£900,000, $1.2m).

Ingrid Carlberg, permanent secretary of the Swedish Academy, said she had broken the news to Carson on the phone shortly before the public announcement.

"She had time to tell me was that she is, for the moment, in Iceland, where she is listening to the wind," Carlberg, said.

"She was taken by surprise but very happy. I could hear that in her voice."

World.title: Venezuela's ex-leader Nicolás Maduro charged with conspiracy to commit torture
World.content:
Prosecutors in the United States have accused Venezuela's former leader NicolÃ¡s Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, of conspiracy to commit torture.

The fresh charges against the couple were made public on Thursday and are in addition to the drug-trafficking and weapons charges already brought against them, which they have denied.

Maduro, 63, and Flores, 69, have been in custody since January in a detention centre in Brooklyn, where they were taken after US forces seized them in a pre-dawn raid on their compound in the Venezuelan capital, Caracas.

Barry J Pollack, Maduro's attorney, said his client denies the new charges and looks forward to his day in court.

Federal prosecutors also announced on Thursday that Flores was added to the earlier narco-terrorism charge.

The trial for both Maduro and Flores is set to begin in June 2027.

Both are being held in a detention centre in Brooklyn and are expected to remain there after Flores's request to be moved to house arrest was denied by a judge on Thursday.

The new accusations relate to the alleged torture of US citizens who were being held in Venezuela while Maduro was in power.

The superseding indictment unsealed on Thursday accuses the former presidential couple of "entrenching themselves in power" by presiding "over a system of repression that relied on violence against political opposition, arbitrary detention, and the torture of detainees, including United States citizens".

According to the indictment, the torture included "electric shock, asphyxiation, rape, forced nudity, prolonged isolation, starvation, punishment cells, and psychological torture".

The prosecutors allege that the psychological torture included threats to kill victims' families, including children.

"All of this was done to ensure that Maduro and Flores retained their power," prosecutors said outside the courthouse on Thursday.

"This conduct, we allege, has caused significant harm to Americans, to US citizens", prosecutors said, calling it "the epitome of corruption".

World.title: Reps warn participating institutions against manipulating NELFUND loans
World.content:
The House of Representatives Committee on Student Loans, Scholarships and Higher Education Financing has warned universities and other beneficiary institutions against withholding funds disbursed under the Federal Government’s student loan scheme.

The committee said some institutions had failed to properly administer funds released by the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) for verified student beneficiaries.

The committee chairman, Ifeoluwa Ehindero (APC, Ondo), disclosed this in a statement on Thursday, following the committee’s recent monitoring activities and engagements with beneficiary institutions.

According to Mr Ehindero, the committee identified instances of institutions withholding NELFUND funds meant for students, delaying refunds to students who had already paid their tuition before the fund’s disbursement, or refunding only part of the amount due to eligible beneficiaries.

He said these practices raised serious concerns about compliance with the rules governing the loan scheme’s administration.

“It is important to state that such practices constitute serious compliance concerns, undermine transparency and accountability, erode students’ confidence in the system and may threaten equitable access to funding for higher education,” Mr Ehindero said.

He also warned that prolonged delays in processing payment notifications and refunds “may also disrupt academic progress and compound the financial hardship faced by affected students.”

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Ehindero urged heads of beneficiary institutions to ensure bursars, directors of ICT, and NELFUND desk officers strictly comply with the financial and administrative requirements for managing funds released under the scheme.

He said institutions must ensure that funds received from NELFUND on behalf of students are promptly and fully applied for the purposes for which they were released.

The committee also directed institutions to refund students who had already paid their fees before NELFUND disbursed funds.

It warned that institutions found deliberately refusing to comply with the scheme’s requirements could face sanctions.

According to the committee, Section 5.6 of the NELFUND Guidelines provides for measures including the suspension of non-compliant institutions from the scheme, recovery of funds and referral of cases to relevant law enforcement and regulatory agencies.

The committee said it would intensify oversight of beneficiary institutions to strengthen enforcement, improve transparency in handling student loan funds, and ensure greater accountability within the scheme.

It said its oversight was aimed at ensuring that the Federal Government’s efforts to make higher education more accessible and affordable were not undermined by administrative failures at the institutional level.

The committee’s warning comes against the backdrop of student complaints about delays in receiving refunds for tuition fees they paid before NELFUND disbursements.

In May, Premium Times reported that some University of Calabar students raised concerns over delayed refunds, although the institution said the process was ongoing.

The university’s NELFUND desk officer said refunds were being made in batches and that, at the time, about 3,000 students had been refunded.

NELFUND is the Federal Government’s student financing scheme, established to provide eligible Nigerian students with zero-interest loans to support their education.

The corporate body was established under the Students Loans (Access to Higher Education) Act, 2024, to manage and disburse interest-free student loans to eligible Nigerian students.

READ ALSO: University students raise concerns over delayed NELFUND refunds

It replaced the former Nigerian Education Bank Act and is a core initiative of President Bola Tinubu’s administration, ensuring financial hurdles do not prevent young Nigerians from accessing tertiary education.

Under the scheme, funds are disbursed to beneficiary institutions to cover approved education-related costs for verified students.

Where a student has already paid the relevant fees before NELFUND makes the payment, the institution is expected to refund the student where applicable.

The scheme is intended to reduce the financial burden of higher education and enable more Nigerians to access tertiary education without being excluded because of their inability to pay upfront.

World.title: Oyebanji presents N490.74bn budget proposal for 2027 to Ekiti assembly
World.content:
Ekiti State Governor Biodun Oyebanji on Thursday presented a proposed N490.74 billion budget for the 2027 fiscal year to the state House of Assembly.

Mr Oyebanji presented the appropriation bill, christened the ‘Budget of Sustained Progress and Prosperity,’ at the assembly chamber in Ado-Ekiti, the state capital.

He said the proposal was designed to consolidate his administration’s achievements and lay a foundation for the next four years.

The governor said the budget also aligned with the state’s 30-year development plan covering the period from 2021 to 2051.

He said the proposal comprised N275.68 billion for recurrent expenditure and N215.06 billion for capital expenditure.

Mr Oyebanji said the estimates would provide a framework for sustained development and improved living standards across the state.

The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the budget focuses on six pillars of his administration.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The pillars include education and healthcare; good governance and transparency; arts, culture and tourism; youth and job creation.

Others are infrastructure and industrialisation, as well as agriculture and rural development.

Mr Oyebanji said the proposal would consolidate gains recorded under his administration’s Shared Prosperity Agenda.

He added that it would strengthen ongoing programmes and create opportunities for economic growth across the state.

Earlier, the Speaker of the House of Assembly, Adeoye Aribasoye, commended Mr Oyebanji for presenting the proposed budget.

Mr Aribasoye said the proposal reflected the aspirations and needs of residents expressed during town hall engagements across the three senatorial districts.

He assured that the assembly would subject the proposal to thorough legislative scrutiny before its passage.

He said the review would focus on constitutionality, revenue projections, stakeholder engagement and equitable distribution of projects.

Mr Aribasoye said lawmakers would also assess the balance between recurrent and capital expenditure.

“As we receive this bill today, the assembly will approach its legislative review with patriotism, objectivity, and thoroughness,” he said.

He said lawmakers would ensure equitable distribution of projects across the three senatorial districts and 16 local government areas.

He added that the assembly would also consider the 22 local council development areas in the state.

Mr Aribasoye said the assembly would cooperate with the executive where necessary and demand accountability where required.

He stressed that such scrutiny was not a contradiction but “constitutional democracy at work.”

(NAN)

World.title: Nationwide PVC collection begins Friday as voter register hits 103 million – INEC
World.content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) says nationwide collection of Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) will begin on Friday, as the commission steps up preparations for the 2027 general elections.

INEC also stated that the number of registered voters had risen to more than 103 million after the completion of the three-phase Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) exercise.

The commission’s chairman, Joash Amupitan, disclosed this on Thursday at the 10th annual conference of the Guild of Corporate Online Publishers (GOCOP) in Lagos.

Mr Amupitan, who is a professor and Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN), was represented at the conference by the Lagos Resident Electoral Commissioner, Ayobami Salami, who delivered his keynote address.

“Nationwide PVC collection will officially commence tomorrow, Friday, 9 October 2026,” Mr Salami, a professor, said.

He stated that 10,772,421 new voters were registered during the three phases of the CVR.

According to him, the new registrations had undergone biometric verification and INEC had completed the final Automated Biometric Identification System (ABIS) cleanup of the register.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The commission has scheduled the preliminary display of the register from 9 to 15 October for voters to check their details and raise claims or objections where necessary.

INEC introduces printable PVCs

Mr Amupitan explained that INEC had introduced printable PVC technology to reduce the time voters would spend waiting for their cards.

He said the technology would also make it easier to replace cards that had been lost or stolen.

The commission, he added, had audited its technological infrastructure and procured new devices ahead of the 2027 elections.

INEC is also strengthening its cybersecurity system and deploying artificial intelligence tools to identify and respond to possible threats to the electoral process.

The commission had earlier announced the acquisition of 57,000 new Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) machines for the election.

INEC disagrees with Agbakoba on election projections

The INEC chairman also disagreed with the position of the conference chairman, Olisa Agbakoba, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN), on the media’s reporting of election projections and exit polls.

Mr Agbakoba had questioned whether restrictions on such reports would be consistent with the constitutional rights to freedom of expression and access to information.

Mr Amupitan noted that people and organisations were free to express opinions and make predictions, but that official election results could only be declared by the appropriate electoral officers.

“I want to respectfully disagree with your position. The position of the law, as we understand it today, is that only the returning officer has the constitutional responsibility to declare results,” he said.

“Opinion is free, but facts are sacred.”

He warned that unofficial declarations could create confusion and trigger a crisis.

Mr Amupitan urged the media to rely on verified results uploaded through INEC’s Result Viewing platform, IReV, when reporting election results.

He also appealed to online publishers to avoid unverified information and clickbait that could mislead voters.

Panel questions INEC’s readiness

The issue of election projections also came up during a panel discussion on “2027 Elections: Trust, Transparency and Shared Responsibilities”.

The panel included the Commissioner of Police in charge of Election Planning, Monitoring and Evaluation, Abayomi Shogunle; Head of Mass Communication at the University of Lagos, Tayo Popoola; Creative Director of Gender Agenda and founder of WEWE Network Afrique, Adaora Sydney-Jack; and Executive Director of the International Press Centre, Lanre Arogundade.

Mr Arogundade urged INEC to give the public more information about the technology it plans to use in 2027.

He said journalists should scrutinise the companies supplying the technology as well as the safeguards put in place to prevent manipulation.

He also questioned the preparedness of political parties to monitor the technology and the wider electoral process.

According to him, any interruption in the electronic transmission of results could become a problem if INEC did not communicate quickly with the public.

He therefore called for a 24-hour crisis communication system that would allow the commission to respond to problems as they emerge.

On election projections, Mr Arogundade said the media should not be prevented from analysing results where the analysis was based on verified polling-unit results already available to the public.

Media urged to understand election laws

Mr Popoola said journalists must understand both media and electoral laws when covering elections.

He noted that the constitutional right to receive and share information did not remove the responsibility of journalists to follow professional and legal standards.

He also raised concerns about media ownership and commercial interests, saying these could influence the way elections are covered.

Ms Sydney-Jack said technology would not by itself restore Nigerians’ confidence in elections.

“Technology cannot substitute institutional credibility,” she said.

She said the election process started long before election day, including political party primaries, candidate selection and campaigns.

According to her, many Nigerians were willing to vote but remained unsure whether their votes would count.

She called for closer scrutiny of party primaries and greater participation by women and young people.

She also warned against the use of security agencies to serve political interests instead of protecting voters.

Police outline security plans

Mr Shogunle said the police had begun preparations for the 2027 elections and were using a more analytical approach to election security.

He said the force had developed state-specific operational plans based on the security challenges in each state.

He explained that the police were also using predictive analysis to guide deployment.

“Election security is not limited to election day,” he said.

Mr Shogunle cited recent elections in Anambra, the Federal Capital Territory and Ekiti as examples of the police’s evolving approach to election security.

He said the police had enough personnel for deployment to polling units and urged civil society organisations and the media to continue providing information that could help identify potential threats.

Speakers call for prosecution of electoral offenders

The panel also raised concerns about the prosecution of electoral offenders.

Speakers questioned why some people arrested during elections were not prosecuted, saying failure to punish offenders could encourage others to commit similar offences.

They called for people found culpable of electoral offences to be prosecuted regardless of their political affiliation.

The discussion also touched on vote buying.

The panellists said inducements were not limited to cash and could include food, livestock and other material items.

They called for stronger enforcement of electoral laws to curb the practice.

The panellists also called for voter education materials to be made available in Nigeria’s major indigenous languages.

They said relying heavily on English could make electoral information inaccessible to some voters.

Hausa, Igbo and Yoruba were mentioned as languages that could be used alongside other indigenous languages to explain voting procedures, electoral rules and voters’ rights.

The speakers also stressed the importance of trained party agents at polling units.

They said properly trained agents could monitor voting, check election materials and observe the completion of polling-unit result forms.

The conference brought together publishers, journalists, electoral officials, security agencies and other stakeholders to discuss preparations for the 2027 elections.

World.title: Similarities between Benin and Opobo, By Eric Teniola
World.content:
Opobo Kingdom in Rivers State now has a new King. He is King Charles Douglas MacPepple Jaja, Jeki VI. The king was crowned as the sixth Amanyanabo of Opobo and the coronation which was held at Jaja Square, Opobo Town, marked the climax of activities that began on September 17, 2026, to celebrate the emergence of the new monarch and the rich cultural heritage of the historic Opobo Kingdom.

The colourful ceremony was attended by former President Goodluck Ebele Jonathan (68) GCFR and his wife, representatives of Rivers State Governor, Siminalayi Fubara; the Obi of Onitsha, Nnayelugo Alfred Nnaemeka Achebe; representatives of the Bayelsa State Government; the Amanyanabo of Grand Bonny Kingdom; representatives of the Rivers State Council of Traditional Rulers; the Olu of Warri; the Dean of Agbor; the Obong of Calabar; members of the Ijaw National Congress and other dignitaries.

King Charles was born in 1959 into the royal family of Opobo. He was crowned by Emmanuel Oko-Jaja, Bishop of the Niger Delta Diocese.

The coronation comes more than 150 years after the establishment of Opobo Kingdom, one of the historic Ibani kingdoms of the Niger Delta.

The kingdom emerged from a political conflict in Grand Bonny in 1869, when Chief Jack Jaja Annie Pepple, known in Ibani tradition as Juwojuwo, and members of the Opubo Annie Pepple group departed Bonny and established a new settlement near the Imo River estuary.

The 25th of December, 1870 is traditionally recognised as the date of the establishment of Opobo Kingdom, with Jaja becoming its first Amanyanabo.

Under King Jaja, Opobo developed into a major political and commercial power in the Oil Rivers region, particularly through the palm produce trade.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

I expected a more huge crowd at the coronation because of the importance of Opobo, especially in the South South region.

The Opobo/ Nkoro LGA of Rivers State is made up of two Ijaw Clans known as Opobo and Nkoro Clans with different communities under them.

The Opobo Clan is of the Ibani- Ijaw subgroup of the Ijaw tribe. Nkoro Clan is of the Okrika -Ijaw subgroup of the Ijaw tribe. Bonny Clan have 75 villages and settlements. Opobo Clan have 20 villages and settlements. Both are of the Ibani subgroup of the Ijaw tribe. Ijaw have 86 Clans and the single largest Ijaw Clan.is Egbema Clan with over 350 villages and settlements under it.

Opobo has the highest literacy rate in Niger delta. Opobo has the highest concentration of professors in Niger Delta. The first set of graduates from university of Ibadan had many Opobo people. Over 60 % of the families in Opobo send their kids overseas for studies and this behavior started far back as 18th century when the children of nobles were sent to England to acquire western education through Opobo seaport.

Their men are well mannered because in Opobo culture, mannerism is imbibed. Secondly, they are mostly educated and polished. They behave like the British because of their long relationship with the British centuries ago and thirdly, they excel in life on the average, Opobo people have quality human resources.

Prominent Opobo indigenes include Governor Amaopusenibo Siminalayi Fubara, the current governor of Rivers state, General (rtd) Kenneth Minimah (67), former Chief of Army Staff, Chief Atedo Peterside (71), founder of Stanbic IBTC Bank Plc, Adawari Pepple, businessman and former Senator, Professor Millar Jaja, the first Orthopaedic Surgeon in West Africa, Professor Sylvanus Cookey, retired vice chancellor of the University of Port-Harcourt, Chief Dagogo Jaja, former Managing Director of Daily Times, Captain Horace Millar Jaja, an Airline Captain and many more.

The history of Opobo is similar to that of Benin Empire. They had rulers who resisted the British Empire many years ago.

Ovonramwen, Oba of Benin was the independent ruler of the Edo Kingdom of Benin. Ovonramwen is renowned for his brave stand against the colonisation of his Kingdom by the British, for which he is generally regarded as the last great king of Southern Nigeria in nineteenth century who attempted to stem the tide of British occupation and conquest.

During the nine years (1888-1897) he reigned, he sought to preserve the sovereignty of the Edo empire as well as its economic interests which, in the end, led to the British armed invasion of Benin in 1897. The Oba lost the battle and was dethroned and banished into exile for life, while his Kingdom was merged into a wider political unit under the British administration. By 1912 that unit, the Protectorate of Southern Nigeria, has been fused with the Protectorate of Northern Nigeria to become the entity of Nigeria.

“Ovonramwen fell for the same reasons as other great African rulers of the late nineteenth century who represented an age that was fast fading away under the determined thrust of the white man resolved to take over the political and economic control of the African coast and the interior—Pepple of Bonny in 1854, Jaja of Opobo in 1887, Nana the Itsekiri in 1894, King Prempeh of Ashanti in January 1896” writes the Professor of History, Philip A. Igbafe in his book, Benin Under British Administration.

Indeed, by the late 1880s during Ovonramwen’s father Adolo’s reign, Britain had already mapped out Benin state as its area of influence. That was reflected in the visit of Captain HL Gallway, the British Commissioner and Vice-Consul of the Benin District of the Oil Rivers Protectorate, to Benin in 1892, four years after Ovonramwen succeeded his father as Oba.

During that visit the British officer signed a treaty with Ovonramwen, for commercial relations between Benin and Britain. Among other clauses the 1892 treaty requested the Oba to co-operate with Britain in the interest of “order, good government and the general progress of civilization”.

The implications of these, as later events were to show, were not fully explained to the Oba of Benin. Because for several years after the treaty Oba Ovonramwen continued to rule his state in the tradition of his ancestors, refusing to “compromise his independence in order to pander too the needs of British officials and traders”, says Igbafe, adding that “relationship between Benin and the traders on the coast as well as with the British officials during those last two decades of the nineteenth century was particularly productive of friction from the British standpoint. This stage was thus being set for the overthrow of Benin”.

It was against that background that Vice-Consul James R. Philips, going against warnings about the provocation such a visit would cause in Benin, embarked on a mission to assess the strength of the Benin Army, and visited Oba Ovonramwen on 18 January, 1897. Phillips and a large number of his men were ambushed outside the city, to which the British responded with the punitive expedition of February 1897. Benin fell in that battle and its Oba was dethroned and deported to Calabar where he died seventeen years later in 1914.

Oba Ovonramwen reigned at a precarious time in the history of Benin. He succeeded to an empire that was on its decline, “probably because of attacks by other indigenous powers on the peripheral peoples of his Empire, which led invariably to a shrinkage of his dominions and possibly too of his throne”. As Idugbowa, Oba Ovonramwen had to fight off opposition to his accession to the throne of his father in 1888; even after that he could only consolidate his rule through purges and executions.

Yet Oba Ovonramwen was determined from the beginning to make his reign as purposeful as possible by maintaining court in the tradition of his ancestors which he hoped to preserve. The human sacrifices at which the British protested were part tradition which the Oba could not abandon. He lost his throne and power in the bid to defend that tradition against foreign aggression. One result of the aggression was the looting of vast quantities of Benin’s excellent works of art, now scattered over the world.

In 1914, the monarchy was restored under Oba Ovonramwen’s eldest son, Eweka II, who was succeeded in turn, in 1933, by Akenzua II.

Let us now look at the Jaja, King of Opobo. He was famous for his resistance to the imposition of colonial domination. He was a slave sold into house of Anna Pepple of Bonny and rose to the headship of his master’s “house.” He later established himself as the most dominant figure in the politics of the Delta states when he became King of the newly founded Kingdom of Opobo. Succession to the headship of an Ijaw trading “house” was not based on heredity but on one’s ability to provide for the welfare of the members of the house. Jaja’s accession to the headship around 1869 caused resentment in other members of the Anna Pepple house. This culminated in a civil war from which Jaja emerged the victor.

After the civil war in Bonny, Jaja led his house to the Opobo river where he founded the Kingdom of Opobo. Here his business acumen and capacity found full scope; he soon established plantations and built a port and strategically placed trading settlements on the creeks which not only enabled him to control the supply of palm oil to the European merchants along the coast but also made Opobo one of the richest Delta states.

With the wealth came political influence and military power. Such was the strength of Jaja’s army that during the Ashanti war he committed a contingent of his soldiers to the British effort, for which he was awarded a sword of honour by Queen Victoria in 1875.

In 1870, having consolidated his new settlement, he proclaimed Opobo an independent state consisting of 14 of the 18 houses of Bonny. Three years later the new state was recognised by Britain which in 1884 entered into a “treaty” with Opobo, placing the latter under the protection of the British Crown. However, the proclamation of a British Protectorate over the Oil Rivers in 1885 not only heralded the demise of the independence of the coast city-states but also precipitated a quarrel between Jaja and the British.

Jaja was the only ruler in the Delta area who questioned the new political order by seeking a definition of the word “protectorate” from the British, who replied vaguely that Her Majesty’s Government would only extend to his kingdom her “gracious favour and protection.” He accepted the explanation, believing that Opobo’s new relationship with Britain would not affect its independence. Accordingly, he continued to monopolise the oil trade, forbidding anyone to deal directly with European merchants on the coast while continuing his direct exports to Britain. As a result, Jaja saw the British insistence on “free” trade as interference and a violation of the 1884 treaty.

The British Consul in Oil Rivers, Harry Johnston, was opposed to Jaja’s continued independence. In 1887, Jonston abrogated his power to impose customs duties on oil exports from the state. Jaja sent a delegation to London to protest to the Secretary of State for the Colonies. Meanwhile Consul Johnston had written to the British Government requesting permission to expel Jaja who had requested successive threats to compel him to meet British demands. The King was “invited” on board a British gunboat, HMS Goshwk, to meet Consul Johnston. Jaja was reassured by Johnston on the eve of their meeting that “I hereby assure you that whatever you accept or reject my proposals tomorrow no restraint whatever will be put on you – –you will be free to go as soon as you have heard the message of the government”.

But once on board, Jaja was asked to choose between being tried for violating the treaty and seeing Opobo bombed by the British Navy. The King opted for trial, which was then held in Accra, Ghana. He was found guilty and banished in 1887 to the West Indies on a pension of 800pounds per annum. This paved the way for the establishment of an effective colonial authority over the region which in the first year provided nearly 90,000 from import duties alone.

King Jaja’s deportation caused much discontent in the Oil Rivers states. After repeated appeals to British Government, the Colonial Secretary set up a commission to investigate and make recommendations for the administration of the new policy. In 1891, the commission, headed by Major Claude MacDonad, recommended that, in response to popular demand in Opobo, King Jaja should be returned and reinstated. In the same year, King Jaja was allowed to return, but on the way back died on 7 July, 1891. His body was subsequently transported to Opobo where it was buried.

There are some countries that fought wars before achieving their independence. I have in mind the Mahdist war fought in Sudan between the British and Egypt. The Xhosa wars between Xhosa kingdom and the British Empire. The Algerian war between France and Algeria, the Dahomey war between Dahomey kingdom and France. The Battle of Mbwila between Congo and Portugal. The Mau Mau rebellion (1952–1960), also known as the Kenya Emergency, was a brutal guerrilla war fought between the Kenya Land and Freedom Army and British colonial forces. The Kenya Land and Freedom Army (KLFA) were led by Dedan Kimathi.

KLFA members mostly belonged to the Kikuyu ethnic group, although there was a great number of people from the Meru, Maasai and Kamba people, among others.

The Rhodesian Bush War was a civil war between three forces: the Zimbabwe African National Liberation Army (ZANLA), the military wing of ZANU led by Robert Mugabe; the Zimbabwe People’s Revolutionary Army (ZIPRA), of ZAPU and Joshua Nkomo, and the Rhodesian Security Forces of Ian Smith.

The Anglo-Zulu War was fought between the Zulu Kingdom and Britain. It had many bloody battles; Britain lost more soldiers than usual for colonial wars.

Britain wanted to war against the Zulu Kingdom so that it could control the region and use African labour in sugar plantations and mines.

In December of 1878, Sir Bartle Frere sent an ultimatum to the Zulu King Cetshwayo. The king did not accept it and Britain invaded the Zulu Kingdom.

The Anglo-Zulu War lasted close to six months, from January to July 1879. It took place in the Zulu Kingdom which is in northeastern modern-day South Africa.

The Maji Maji Rebellion was war between various peoples in Tanzania and Germany.

During colonialism Germans forced Tanzanians to labour for them. Tanzanians had to build their roads and were forced to grow cash crops like cotton for Germans to sell overseas.

Tanzanians warred against the Germans to put a stop to their suffering.

The Maji Maji Rebellion took place on the land of many ethnic groups like the Matumbi and Ngoni peoples in Tanganyika which is now southern Tanzania. It lasted two years, from 1905 to 1907.

After Germany won the Maji Maji Rebellion there was a famine called Ukame, or the Great Hunger because of the scorched-earth policies the governor GA von Götzen used during the war.

It took more independence movements, led by people like Dr Julius Nyerere with TANU for Tanzania to become independent from Britain.

The Rif War was a war between the Rif Republic and Spain, later joined by France. Different Amazigh ethnic groups formed the Rif Republic.

At the Berlin Conference Spain decided that the Rif region was Spanish territory, however, until then Spain had no real power there.

The Rif was rich in high-grade iron, that Spain soon started mining, something that Riffians did not want.

The War of the Golden Stool, or the Fifth Anglo-Ashanti War, was a war between the Ashanti Kingdom and Britain.

The Golden Stool was a royal and sacred throne and the symbol of power in the Ashanti Kingdom.

In 1900, at a meeting with Ashanti leaders, Governor Sir Frederick Mitchell Hodgson, demanded to have the Golden Stool and to sit on it – so that Britain could rule the Ashanti and their land, which was rich in gold.

Soon after, the Ashanti kingdom, led by the Queen Mother Yaa Asantewaa, fought back to protect the Golden Stool.

The War of the Golden Stool lasted 7 months, from March to September 1900. The war took place in the Ashanti Kingdom, in the modern-day Ghana.

The Portuguese Colonial War was a war between various African independence movements and Portugal.

Major movements include the African Party for the Independence of Guinea and Cape Verde (PAIGC), the People’s Movement for the Liberation of Angola (MPLA) and the Mozambique Liberation Front (FRELIMO).

During Portuguese colonialism Africans were forced to work, often with no pay, their land was made into official overseas provinces of Portugal.

Africans fought Portugal to end colonialism and take back their land and freedom. During the Portuguese War most African countries were already independent.

The Portuguese Colonial War was fought during the Cold war between 1961 and 1974, it lasted 13 years.

It took place on three different territories, known as Portuguese Africa at the time, today they are the countries of Angola, Guinea-Bissau and Mozambique.

All three countries became independent from Portugal between 1973 and 1974.

Nigeria is lucky, we did not take part in any military adventure before we got our independence. Our independence was negotiated diplomatically. But some units within the country like Benin, Bonny and Opobo kingdoms experienced brutal British colonisation. The great grandson of Oba Ovonramwen, the current Oba of Benin, Oba Eheneden Erediauwa, Ewuare II, was crowned on 20 October, 2016. King Charles Douglas MacPepple Jaja, Jeki VI of Opobo has just begun an expected long reign. May their era be peaceful and progressive.

Eric Teniola, a former director at The Presidency, wrote from Lagos.

World.title: Abiodun approves J4-Gao Road, sets November for Deep Sea port ground breaking
World.content:
Ogun State Governor, Dapo Abiodun, has approved the construction of the J4-Gao Road in Ogun Waterside Local Government Area as part of measures to open up the axis and provide critical infrastructure to support the emerging investments in the area.

Abiodun disclosed this on Wednesday at an All Progressives Congress (APC) stakeholders’ engagement meeting held in Ibiade, headquarters of Ogun Waterside Local Government Area.

The Governor, who lamented the prolonged neglect of the area by successive administrations, said the decision to construct the J4-Gao Road was informed by the strategic importance of Ogun Waterside to the State’s emerging economic and industrial landscape.

He also disclosed that the Federal Government had approved the construction of a four-kilometre bridge that would connect the local government to the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, describing the development as a major infrastructure intervention that would facilitate access to the area and support the take-off of major investments planned for the axis.

According to him, the proposed infrastructure would complement the development of the Gateway Deep Sea Port and the Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) project, both of which are expected to significantly alter the economic profile of Ogun Waterside and strengthen the State’s position in the maritime, energy and logistics sectors.

Abiodun expressed appreciation to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for supporting the development of the Deep Sea Port and other strategic projects in the area, saying the projects would position Ogun State as a major energy, maritime and international trade hub.

He announced that the groundbreaking ceremony for the Deep Sea Port had been scheduled for November, with construction expected to commence before the end of the year and be completed by 2030.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Abiodun said the development of the port was the culmination of sustained efforts by his administration to create an enabling environment for large-scale investments, stressing that the administration had consistently pursued infrastructure and policy interventions designed to make Ogun more attractive to investors.

He noted that the Deep Sea Port and associated investments would create significant employment and business opportunities, particularly for young people and residents of Ogun Waterside.

The Governor therefore urged youths in the area to acquire the skills and competencies required to take advantage of the opportunities that would emerge from the projects.

“These projects will change the economic fortunes of Ogun Waterside. Our young people must begin to prepare themselves now to take advantage of the opportunities that will come with these investments,” he said.

Abiodun noted that the strategic investments in the area were expected to generate more than 50,000 direct employment opportunities, while also creating extensive opportunities across logistics, transportation, construction, hospitality, services, manufacturing and other sectors.

The Governor said the development of the Deep Sea Port would also complement Ogun’s growing industrial base and strategic location within the Lagos-Ogun economic corridor, further strengthening the State’s reputation as Nigeria’s industrial capital.

He described Ogun Waterside as strategically important to the State, noting that the local government has 126 polling units and about 62,000 registered voters.

Abiodun urged residents and APC members in the area to remain united and sustain their support for the party, saying continued political stability and support would help consolidate the gains recorded by the APC-led administrations at the State and Federal levels.

He called on party members to intensify mobilisation ahead of the 2027 general elections and urged voters to support APC candidates across the ballot, from the presidential election to the State House of Assembly.

The Governor assured the people that continued support for the party would strengthen the prospects for sustained development and effective representation.

Speaking at the event, the APC Presidential and Governorship Campaign Director-General, Senator Lekan Mustapha, urged residents to protect the development gains recorded in the area under the APC-led government.

Mustapha cautioned against taking political decisions that could jeopardise the ongoing transformation, urging the people to remain committed to the party and its candidates in the 2027 elections.

Also speaking, a former Commissioner for Education, Science and Technology, Prof. Segun Awonusi, commended Abiodun for what he described as his role in driving the development taking place in Ogun Waterside.

Awonusi expressed confidence that the people of the area would reciprocate the administration’s interventions with massive support for the APC in the 2027 elections.

World.title: NSC reshuffles sports federations’ secretaries
World.content:
The National Sports Commission (NSC) has reshuffled the General Secretaries of some national sports federations as part of efforts to strengthen their administration and improve operations.

The Director General of the NSC, Bukola Olopade, announced the changes during a meeting with General Secretaries of the national sports federations in Abuja.

Mr Olopade commended the secretaries for their professionalism, commitment and sacrifices toward the development of Nigerian sports, as well as their support for the commission since the appointment of the current leadership led by Chairman Shehu Dikko and himself as Director General.

He said the reshuffling was intended to strengthen the administration and operations of the affected federations in line with the government’s sports development agenda.

“Let me be clear that no secretary is being removed because he or she has been sacked. They are only being posted to another federation to carry out another assignment. This is how much the Chairman, Mallam Shehu Dikko, and I believe in all our secretaries and their professional expertise,” Mr Olopade said.

He added: “I have always said that the secretaries are the lifeline of our sports. They play a very critical role in the fulfilment of our mandate at the NSC to statutorily regulate and develop sports in the country, in line with the mandate of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR.”

Under the new arrangement, Bunmi Oluode becomes the Secretary General of the Athletics Federation, replacing Israel Inwang, who has been posted to the Padel Federation.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Rita Mosindi has been appointed Acting Secretary General of the Basketball Federation, while Amina Amanchi, the former Secretary General, has been posted to the Rowing Federation.

Tosin Samuel is the new Secretary General of the Shooting Federation, while Tinuoso Dolapo becomes Secretary General of the Karate Federation.

Javan Bennard has been assigned as Secretary General of the Fencing Federation, while Dorothy Okpo becomes Secretary General of the Arm Wrestling Federation.

The NSC said the reshuffling was aimed at deploying its administrative personnel more strategically and strengthening the effectiveness of the national sports federations.

The changes were announced on 8 October 2026.

World.title: Fuel subsidy would cost Nigeria over N20trn yearly — Minister
World.content:
The Federal Government has rejected calls for the return of petrol subsidy, warning that subsidising fuel could cost the country more than N20 trillion annually and ultimately make petrol more expensive.

The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, disclosed this on Thursday during a press briefing in Abuja on rising petrol prices and the subsidy debate.

Mr Oyedele said Nigeria consumes about 50 million litres of petrol daily, meaning that returning petrol to its pre-2023 reform price would cost more than N20 trillion every year.

He said even a proposal to sell petrol at N500 per litre would cost the government more than N16 trillion annually, before accounting for increased consumption and smuggling.

“Amounts of that size are nearly everything the Federation Account shared among all three tiers of government in 2025,” Mr Oyedele said.

He warned that funding such a subsidy would come at the expense of other government responsibilities, including salaries, pensions, schools, hospitals and security.

The minister’s comment comes amid renewed calls for the reintroduction of fuel subsidy, with the issue increasingly featuring in political debates ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

‘Subsidy could push petrol to N2,000 per litre’

According to the minister, a return to subsidy could weaken government revenues, trigger a sovereign credit downgrade, increase borrowing costs and put pressure on foreign reserves and the naira.

The government estimates that the exchange rate could approach N3,000 to the dollar within months if subsidy is restored.

Mr Oyedele said this could push the price of so-called subsidised petrol to at least ₦2,000 per litre, significantly above the current average of about ₦1,400.

“A subsidy does not lower the cost of fuel. It only changes how it is paid, and when,” he said.

He argued that crude oil, freight and refining inputs are largely priced in dollars, meaning that forcing down the naira price of petrol would effectively require the government to subsidise foreign exchange.

‘Production subsidy’ is consumption subsidy

The minister also rejected descriptions of a proposed subsidy for locally refined petrol as a “production subsidy”.

He said a genuine production subsidy would support producers who could not compete at market prices, whereas the proposal being discussed would amount to providing discounted crude that would eventually be passed on to consumers at the pump.

“This is different, it is a discount on crude, passed through to the pump. That is a consumption subsidy by another route, with the same bill attached,” he said.

Mr Oyedele said subsidised fuel would also increase the price differential between Nigeria and neighbouring countries, potentially encouraging smuggling and effectively making Nigerian taxpayers subsidise motorists in other countries.

N15.8trn saved from subsidy removal

The minister defended the 2023 removal of petrol subsidy, saying it had released N15.8 trillion to the Federation Account between June 2023 and December 2025.

Of that amount, N10.4 trillion went to states and local governments, he said.

Mr Oyedele said 27 states could not reliably pay salaries in May 2023, but that none was in that position at the time of the briefing.

At the federal level, he said about two-thirds of the subsidy savings, combined with additional independent revenue and borrowing, had been used for spending that directly benefited Nigerians through higher wages, infrastructure, electricity subsidy and social transfers.

The remaining funds, he said, were used to stabilise the economy, particularly as the cost of servicing debt increased due to higher interest rates introduced to tackle inflation.

Government rejects blanket subsidy

Mr Oyedele said the government had instead used tax and duty waivers, local refining, naira-for-crude arrangements, exchange-rate stabilisation and CNG deployment to moderate fuel costs.

He said the government had granted a full waiver of taxes and duties on petrol worth more than N3.3 trillion for the year to 30 September 2026.

He added that the government would continue to consider targeted relief rather than a blanket subsidy.

Among the new measures are a 30-day discount on petrol sold at NNPC stations, a proposed N1,350 ceiling on the ex-gantry or landing cost of petrol, additional cash transfers, subsidised credit and faster CNG deployment.

The government is also considering an excess profit tax on energy operators, with proceeds earmarked for measures to cushion vulnerable consumers.

Mr Oyedele said the government would not reverse the subsidy reform, arguing that doing so would expose Nigeria to the same cycle of fuel scarcity, smuggling, currency weakness and fiscal pressure experienced in the past.

“Our task is not to reverse a necessary reform designed to set our country on the path towards sustained prosperity,” he said. “It is to make sure its gains reach more Nigerians, more quickly and in more tangible ways.”

World.title: OK Movement makes U-turn on campaign council, blames APC for crisis
World.content:
The OK Movement has acknowledged that its recently disowned presidential campaign council (PCC) was created without adherence to due process.

The spokesperson of OK Movement, Emmanuel Idakwo, disclosed this on Thursday when he appeared as a guest on Sunrise Daily, a Channels TV’s breakfast programme.

“The issue of a campaign council that was allegedly published by some individuals claiming to be members of the OK Movement. But I can assure you that that was not done officially.

“Because even Peter Obi had no knowledge of it. And it’s not possible for any member of the OK Movement to officially do such without his knowledge. So, it was not officially done. There was a motive behind it,” he said.

The OK (short for Obi-Kwankwaso) Movement is one of the independent groups mobilising support for the 2027 presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, and his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso.

Recall that the leadership of the NDC and the OK Movement appeared to have been in a face-off after the party disowned a PCC unveiled by the support group.

In response, the support group rejected the NDC’s position, insisting that it does not require the personal validation or approval of any individual within the NDC before exercising its legitimate organisational functions.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

‘Not by official leadership’

Mr Idakwo stressed that the OK Movement has a cordial relationship with the NDC and its National Leader, Seriake Dickson.

The spokesperson argued that every action and statements made by a supposed supporter of Mr Obi especially on social media are often ascribed to the OK Movement.

He suggested that the creation of the PCC and other remarks attributed to the OK Movement were “never done by any official leadership” of the support group.

“There is no official leadership of either the Obidient Movement, the Kwankwasiya, the OK Movement

that has ever come up to say that they are against the NDC structure or the party leadership.

“So, anyone who says these things online claiming to be members of these groups, I can tell you they are not verified to be part of the leadership of the groups,” he said.

‘APC stoking crisis in the NDC to discredit party’

Mr Idakwo alleged that the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) had been doing “everything” to discredit the NDC.

“I will tell you quite frankly that everything that is possible to be thrown at the NDC to reduce the credibility of the party or reduce the level of sensitisation that is rapidly growing with supporters is being done by the ruling party,” he claimed.

The spokesperson insisted that the APC had been stoking the crisis in the NDC by amplifying minor issues such as the campaign council controversy to create an impression that the opposition party was divided.

“I believe that if you look at the stories on the internet, the comments from individuals, you would see that these issues are being amplified equally by supporters of the APC just to discredit our NDC to make it look like the NDC is divided,” he alleged.

APC silent

When contacted on Thursday for comments on the allegations, the spokesperson of the APC, Felix Morka, asked a PREMIUM TIMES reporter to forward his questions via a text message.

But Mr Morka was yet to respond to the questions as of the time of this report.

Background

There had been a face-off between the NDC leadership and members of OK Movement over setting up of the PCC for the 2027 election.

PREMIUM TIMES reported that, on 17 September, the OK Movement constituted a 59-member PCC to mobilise support for Messrs Obi and Kwankwaso ahead of the 2027 election.

The support group claimed the PCC would operate independent of the PCC to be inaugurated by the NDC.

READ ALSO: Police arrest OK Movement coordinator during Independence Day march in Uyo

But the NDC disowned the support group, maintaining that the party would soon unveil its PCC for the 2027 election.

It warned the support group that their action could destabilise the party.

However, the support group, in response, rejected the NDC’s position, insisting that it does not require the personal validation or approval of any individual within the party before exercising its legitimate organisational functions in accordance with established processes.

The NDC later gave Messrs Obi and Kwankwaso the power to nominate choice leaders of the party’s soon-to-be unveiled PCC.

World.title: APC campaign organisation alleges attacks in Oyo
World.content:
By Adeola Badru

IBADAN — The Senator Sharafadeen Alli Campaign Organisation (SSACO) has alleged attacks on All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates, supporters and political activities in Ibadan, Oyo State.

The organisation alleged that Alhaja Tawakalitu Alli, wife of the APC governorship candidate, Sharafadeen Alli, was attacked during a medical outreach she organised at Ibikunle House, Ayeye, Ibadan.

It also alleged that the campaign teams of the APC candidate for Oyo South Senatorial District, Aderemi Oseni, and the party’s candidate for Ibadan North-West/Ibadan South-West Federal Constituency, Folake Olunloyo-Oshinowo, were attacked during separate campaign events at Agbaje Market, Orita-Merin, and Idi-Arere, Ibadan.

In a statement issued by its Director of Media and Publicity, Bisi Oladele, SSACO described the alleged incidents as attempts to disrupt political activities ahead of the 2027 elections.

The organisation called on Governor Seyi Makinde and the Allied Peoples Movement (APM) governorship candidate, Bimbo Adekanmbi, to ensure that political actors are allowed to campaign freely.

“The SSACO is at the least miffed by the unwarranted and barbaric attacks by Allied People’s Movement (APM) hoodlums on Alhaja Tawakalitu Alli during a medical outreach she organised at Ibikunle House, Ayeye, Ibadan, on Wednesday,” the statement said.

It further alleged that Oseni and Olunloyo-Oshinowo were attacked during separate campaign events in the city.

SSACO said the alleged incidents would not force the APC to suspend its campaign activities, stressing that its candidates and supporters were entitled to associate, assemble and campaign within the law.

“The SSACO calls on Governor Seyi Makinde and the party’s governorship candidate, Hon. Bimbo Adekanmbi, to rein in on their supporters,” it said.

The organisation also called on security agencies to investigate the alleged attacks, identify those responsible and prosecute them where appropriate.

“The SSACO calls on security agencies to fish out these perpetrators of violence and bring them to book in order to serve justice to the victims and also serve as a deterrence to violence in our dear state,” it said.

SSACO further urged the state government to protect residents irrespective of their political affiliations, saying the alleged attacks posed a threat to peaceful political participation.

“As the chief security officer of the state, Governor Makinde carries the responsibility to protect all residents irrespective of their political leanings,” the organisation said.

The campaign organisation alleged that the incidents were connected to tensions ahead of the 2027 elections, but provided no independent evidence in the statement to substantiate its allegation that the governor or Adekanmbi sponsored the attacks.

It also urged political parties to focus on issue-based campaigns and policy proposals rather than violence.

“The good people of Oyo State deserve issue-based campaigns, not violence. We advise Governor Makinde, Adekanmbi and other political parties to focus on presenting their programmes and policies to the electorate,” SSACO said.

The organisation maintained that the alleged attacks would not deter APC candidates from campaigning across the state.

World.title: AELEX plays key role in Dangote Refinery’s $1.5bn IPO
World.content:
By Henry Ojelu

LAGOS — The approximately US$1.5 billion Initial Public Offering, IPO, of Dangote Petroleum Refinery & Petrochemicals FZE has been completed, with AELEX acting as Solicitors to the Offer in the landmark transaction.

The offering is the largest single IPO undertaken in Africa and the first public offering by a Free Zone Entity, FZE, in Nigeria.

In a statement, the management of AELEX said the transaction marked a significant development in Nigeria’s capital market and provided a new route for large-scale businesses operating under the Free Zone framework to access public capital.

According to the firm, the transaction also builds on its longstanding relationship with the Dangote Industries Group.

AELEX said it previously acted as solicitor to the issuer in the N60 billion IPO of Dangote Sugar Refinery Plc.

The firm also said it had advised on other major projects within the group, including the US$798 million syndicated limited-recourse financing for the Obajana Cement Project involving international development and export finance institutions.

The statement added that AELEX advised on aspects of the establishment and operation of the Dangote Refinery project within Nigeria’s Free Zone framework.

On the latest IPO, the management said the offering would broaden public participation in the refinery project while providing an additional source of capital for the industrial development.

It said the transaction also demonstrated the capacity of Nigeria’s capital market to support large-scale industrial projects.

The Dangote Refinery IPO is expected to further widen investment participation in the project and contribute to the development of Nigeria’s capital market.

World.title: HIV status not food safety risk, LSACA tells food sector stakeholder
World.content:
By Henry Ojelu

The Lagos State AIDS Control Agency, LSACA, has urged employers and workers in the food sector to end stigma and discrimination against people living with HIV, stressing that the virus cannot be transmitted through the preparation, handling or serving of food.

The agency made the call at a sensitisation meeting for food handlers and representatives of food-sector associations on HIV-related workplace practices and applicable legal provisions, held Thursday at the STO Resource Centre Hall, CBD, Ikeja.

The meeting was aimed at dispelling misconceptions about HIV transmission and promoting safe, inclusive and non-discriminatory practices in the food sector.

Speaking at the event, the Chief Executive Officer of LSACA, Dr. Folakemi Animashaun, represented by the Director, Projects, Mr. Michael Essien, said there was no scientific basis for excluding people living with HIV from food-related employment.

Animashaun said HIV was not transmitted through handling, preparing or serving food, sharing utensils or through ordinary workplace and social contact.

According to her, “a person’s HIV status does not make them a food-safety risk,” urging food-sector stakeholders to base workplace decisions on scientific evidence rather than fear and misinformation.

She cautioned against using legitimate food-safety and medical fitness requirements as a basis for discriminatory HIV screening or exclusion from employment.

The LSACA boss also stressed the need to protect the confidentiality of workers’ HIV-related information, saying such information must be handled with appropriate consent, respect and dignity.

She noted that stigma and discrimination could discourage people from testing, accessing treatment and using health services for fear of losing their jobs or having their status disclosed without consent.

Animashaun urged food establishments and associations to review their workplace policies to ensure compliance with the principles of confidentiality, informed consent and non-discrimination.

Also speaking, the facilitator, Mr. Tiamiyu Hussein of the Lagos State Safety Commission, stressed the importance of maintaining safe and healthy workplaces without discriminating against workers.

Hussein explained the distinction between legitimate medical fitness assessments for food handlers and HIV screening, urging employers to ensure that occupational health and safety procedures were appropriately implemented.

He further encouraged employers and workers to protect the confidentiality of health information and ensure that no person was subjected to unfair treatment on account of HIV status.

The sensitisation also covered HIV transmission, prevention and treatment, with participants reminded that there is no risk of acquiring HIV from food prepared, handled or served by a person living with the virus.

Participants were encouraged to challenge misconceptions, promote fair employment practices and support appropriate referral and grievance mechanisms across the food sector.

World.title: Lagos 2027: Doherty unveils 34-point manifesto, Animashaun as running mate
World.content:
To review pensions of former governors

By Henry Obetta

THE Lagos State Governorship Candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Mr Funso Doherty, has unveiled a 34-point manifesto he said would take the state to the next level, if elected. He also unveiled Mrs. Tolani Animashaun as his running mate in the February 6, 2027 governorship poll.

Presenting his manifesto titled: Ònà Tuntun (New Road), yesterday, in Lagos, Doherty said the manifesto contained 34 specific commitments across health, education, housing, transport, environment, jobs and small business and honest governance.

Specifically, Doherty, among others, promised to deliver in four years 150,000 homes, provide free healthcare for pregnant women and children under-16, free education through secondary school and technical colleges. He also promised to provide free textbooks, and nutritious meals for students in public schools.

He added: “Then for those children who are in public schools, Lagos State Public Schools, who need to be transported to their school, public transport for children in school uniforms going to their school will be provided.

“The whole objective is that there should be no child in Lagos State that will not benefit from a quality education because his or her parents cannot afford it or because of the circumstances of his or her birth. Because if we don’t, it is our future that we are mortgaging.”

On transportation, Doherty pledged to modernise the state’s transport system, particularly the Red and Blue Line rail networks, by improving connectivity between them. He also promised to establish decentralised road maintenance frameworks across the local governments to ensure more efficient and timely maintenance of roads.

The NDC governorship candidate pledged to run a transparent administration, promising to lead by example and ensure strict enforcement of the Code of Conduct for Public Officers.

He pledged to review all major public-private partnerships, PPPs in Lagos, saying the review would determine whether corrective actions were necessary. He also promised to review public servants’ salaries and allowances to ensure public officers receive reasonable remuneration, arguing that poor pay could undermine efficiency and integrity in the civil service.

The candidate also promised to subject the benefits and packages of former governors to an independent review and make the outcome public.

He further pledged to enforce compliance with government rules and prosecute criminal activity regardless of the position of those involved. “And this applies from the top all the way to the bottom,” he said, adding that his administration would regularly publish its progress and openly acknowledge areas where it fell short.

Doherty also criticised the current Lagos state government, arguing that it had failed to adequately meet the needs of residents despite the state’s substantial financial resources. He said the government should translate its revenue into improved public services and a better quality of life for Lagosians

In her remarks, the NDC deputy governorship candidate, Mrs Tolani Animashaun, pledged to work with Doherty, to build a Lagos where the government prioritises the needs of residents.

Citing her experience in education, finance and community mobilisation, she said the ticket would promote better opportunities for young people, improve education and ensure accountability in the management of public funds.

“Government that works for the people. That is what this team believes in and that is why I am here,” she said, urging residents to support the campaign and “lend us your hand” to achieve our vision for the state.

World.title: Only a madman will vote for Tinubu in 2027 — Amaechi
World.content:
Rotimi Amaechi, vice-presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), has described President Bola Tinubu’s decision to remove the petrol subsidy as “reckless,” declaring that only a madman would vote for the president in the 2027 general election.

Amaechi made the remarks on Thursday at the ADC town hall meeting in Edo State, where he urged Nigerians to reject Tinubu, accusing his administration’s economic policies of worsening hardship across the country.

“I read on social media that it is in 2027 that we will know how many madmen we have in Nigeria. It is only a madman that can vote for Tinubu,” he said.

“If you are not mad, then Tinubu should not win here.”

The former Minister of Transportation also accused supporters of the president of being motivated by self-interest.

Amaechi faulted the removal of the petrol subsidy, rejecting Tinubu’s description of the policy as an act of courage.

He argued that the president’s decision to proceed with the policy despite having been advised against it amounted to recklessness.

“There is a difference between courage and recklessness. Tinubu wasn’t courageous; he was reckless,” Amaechi said.

The ADC chieftain lamented the rising cost of living, saying many Nigerians could no longer afford basic necessities.

“People are not able to feed. Things are difficult,” he said, attributing the hardship faced by households to the administration’s economic policies.

Amaechi also criticised Nigeria’s energy sector, arguing that the country had failed to harness its abundant natural resources to drive industrial production and economic growth.

He noted that Nigeria had substantial crude oil and natural gas reserves, particularly in the South-South region, but had failed to translate its resource wealth into sustainable prosperity for its citizens.

The former minister called for policies that would stimulate domestic production rather than increase the financial burden on consumers and businesses.

He said Atiku Abubakar, the ADC presidential candidate, would introduce production subsidies to strengthen local industries, boost domestic production and ease economic pressure on Nigerians if elected president in 2027.

World.title: Trump rules out new Iran attack before US midterm elections
World.content:
(Photo by Mandel NGAN / AFP)

President Donald Trump on Thursday ruled out attacking Iran before the US midterm elections on November 3, saying Washington was holding “productive discussions” with Tehran.

Trump’s post on his Truth Social platform followed a surge in oil prices on Thursday driven by media reports suggesting potential new US strikes prior to those elections.

“I want to make it clear to everybody that, while Iran is in very bad condition, both Economically and Militarily, and while the Blockade will remain in full force and effect…we will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the Midterm Elections,” he wrote.

“We are having productive discussions with the Islamic Republic of Iran,” he added, without providing additional details.

The Atlantic magazine reported on Wednesday that the White House had asked the Pentagon to develop options to strike Iranian targets that could be used before the midterms. The New York Times published a similar report on Thursday, saying the plans were being developed despite Trump’s “ambivalence”.

The rise in crude oil prices has also been fueled by persistent tensions in the Strait of Hormuz — a strategic chokepoint for the global oil trade — as well as hostilities between Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis and Saudi Arabia.

In a recent sign of those tensions, an oil tanker sailing off the north coast of Qatar reported being struck “by multiple projectiles,” causing an unspecified number of casualties, the UKMTO maritime agency said Wednesday.

Polls suggest that US voters are strongly dissatisfied over rising fuel prices, linked to the conflict launched by the United States and Israel against Iran in February.

The US leader has repeatedly insisted in recent weeks that the United States has effectively won the Iran war, despite ongoing unrest and a recent security threat that forced the withdrawal of American bombers from a base in England.

But Trump’s claims that prices will fall as soon as the Iran war is over have so far fallen on deaf ears with voters.

The midterm elections will shape the final two years of Trump’s presidential term as his Republican Party risks losing its current grip on Congress.

Although Trump is not on the ballot, he is heavily involved in the campaign, holding numerous rallies in an attempt to limit the damage or even turn the political tide.

Trump has warned he faces a possible third impeachment if Democrats retake the House of Representatives, and the White House is preparing for a slew of investigations into corruption and abuse of power.

The US president also on Thursday sought to calm a furor over his comments at a rally earlier this week that Iran could “take out” the cities of Los Angeles and San Diego.

Trump, 80, blamed the “fake and artificial news” for misinterpreting the remarks, which Democrats pounced on.

“In actuality, what I was talking about was that a temporary increase in the price of Gasoline is a small price to pay for Iran not having a Nuclear Weapon and, if you want to see a big price, can you imagine what it would be like if they bombed San Diego and/or Los Angeles?” Trump said on Truth Social.

AFP

World.title: El-Rufai fails to get order stopping ICPC, EFCC from freezing accounts
World.content:
Nasir El-Rufai

By Ikechukwu Nnochiri

Former Governor of Kaduna State, Nasir El-Rufai, has failed to persuade the Federal High Court in Abuja to stop the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) and other anti-graft agencies in the country from freezing his bank accounts.

In a ruling by Justice Joyce Abdulmalik, the court dismissed a suit filed by the former governor, who has been in detention, seeking an order restraining federal government agencies from moving against his assets.

The court held that the suit not only lacked merit but was speculative, as no reasonable cause of action was disclosed against the agencies the applicant listed as defendants.

Therefore, the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), the Department of State Services (DSS) and the Attorney General of the Federation (AGF) were struck out from the case.

In the suit he filed on February 24, El-Rufai prayed the court for an interim injunction directing the respondents to maintain the status quo ante regarding his assets.

According to him, the order was necessary to prevent him from being placed in a state of helplessness. He insisted that the severance pay he received upon completing his tenure as governor of Kaduna State between 2015 and 2023 could not reasonably be suspected to be proceeds of any unlawful activity.

He urged the court to declare that properties purchased from his severance pay were lawfully acquired.
