9 to 11 October: The opening weekend

Friday 9 October, 20:30 One Night of Queen Megarama Casablanca · 350 MAD (about US$35) A Queen tribute show that promises a concert where the audience sings from the first song to the last. The organiser says it is the closest you can get to Queen on stage today. A second night was listed for Thursday 8 October, which has now passed.

Friday 9 October, 20:00 Beethoven l’Exalté, Orchestre Philharmonique du Maroc Théâtre l’Hermitage · 100 MAD (about US$10) The Moroccan Philharmonic Orchestra marks its 30th season with a year devoted to Beethoven, ahead of the 200th anniversary of his death in March 2027. This first programme pairs the Piano Concerto No. 3 with the Seventh Symphony, with Dina Bensaïd as pianist and conductor. The same programme repeats on Saturday 10 October.

Saturday 10 October, 17:00 The Wellness Experience OM Studios, Tahiti Beach · 350 MAD (about US$35) A wellness event at a beachfront venue. It starts at 17:00, so it suits people who want an early evening out.

Saturday 10 October, 20:00 Garou & Tayc, Casa Music Show 2026 Sofitel Casablanca Tour Blanche · Listed at 600 MAD (about US$60) Two francophone singers share one bill. The organiser promises unreleased duets, specially reworked for the night, plus solo performances of their biggest hits. It is the most expensive ticket of the opening weekend.

Saturday 10 October, 20:00 Beethoven l’Exalté, second night Théâtre l’Hermitage · 100 MAD (about US$10) The orchestra repeats Friday’s programme, which makes it the calmer option on a night crowded with pop shows.

Sunday 11 October, time to be confirmed with the venue Candlelight: tribute to Hans Zimmer Hilton Garden Inn Casablanca Sud, Boulevard Zoulikha Nasri · 300 MAD (about US$30) A quartet plays film music by Hans Zimmer by candlelight. The listing shows no start time, so confirm it with the venue before you go.

Sunday 11 October, 21:00 Candlelight: Coldplay and Imagine Dragons Hilton Garden Inn Casablanca Sud, Boulevard Zoulikha Nasri · 300 MAD (about US$30) A quartet performs songs by Coldplay and Imagine Dragons by candlelight. The listing gives 21:00 as the start and 23:59 as the end.

15 to 17 October: Mid-month concerts

Thursday 15 October, 20:30 Nacim Haddad in Casablanca Megarama Casablanca · 250 MAD (about US$25) A weeknight concert at Megarama, the multiplex that also hosts the Queen show.

Saturday 17 October, 20:30 Haj Saïd Berrada & Abir El Abbed, La Grande Rencontre des Voix Marocaines Barceló Anfa · 200 MAD (about US$20) A concert of Moroccan vocal tradition, billed in a listing as an Issawa evening. Issawa is a Sufi musical brotherhood known for its chanting and rhythms.

Saturday 17 October, 20:30 Fehd Benchemsi & The Lalla in concert Megarama Casablanca · 200 MAD (about US$20) A second concert the same evening, so you can choose between a traditional voices night and a contemporary band.

22 to 24 October: Jazz, orchestra and Arabic song

Thursday 22 October, 20:30 MOEUN, jazz concert Studio des Arts vivants · 300 MAD (about US$30) MOEUN presents delicate pieces inspired by nature and emotion, including tracks from their album Intérieurs. It is the month’s main jazz date in our verified listings.

Friday 23 October, 20:30 Amal & Mazzika Orchestra Studio des arts vivants · 250 MAD (about US$25) Conductor and violinist Amal leads an orchestral tribute to timeless Arabic songs. Arrangements stay close to the classics that generations know.

Saturday 24 October, time to be confirmed with the venue Wael Jassar in concert Covered hall, Complexe Mohamed V · 180 MAD (about US$18) The Lebanese singer is known for romantic ballads. The listing shows 18:30 in its details but 21:00 in its description, so confirm the start time with the organiser, Pavillon Culture, before you buy.

29 to 31 October: The closing stretch

Thursday 29 October, 20:00 Coldplay Tribute, A Sky Full of Stars Complexe Mohamed V · 300 MAD (about US$30) An immersive stadium-style tribute show.

Friday 30 October, 20:00 Labess, Mega Concert Complexe Mohammed V · 250 MAD (about US$25) Labess is an Algerian-Canadian band. The organiser describes a large staged concert built to make the whole audience dance.

Friday 30 October, 20:00 Taylor Swift Tribute by Xenna, The Eras Experience Complexe sportif Mohamed V · 150 MAD (about US$15) A tribute show with costumes and choreography, running through songs from Love Story to Anti-Hero. It is on the same evening and at the same complex as Labess, so check which hall your ticket names.

Planning your Casablanca in October

Saturday 31 October 2026 is Unity Day, a new paid national holiday created by royal decision. It marks the UN Security Council resolution on the Sahara adopted on 31 October 2025. Public administrations and private employers are covered by two decrees.

Employees who must work that day receive double pay or compensatory rest. No other national holiday falls between 9 and 31 October 2026. The next one is the Green March on Friday 6 November.

From 9 October, the headline dates are One Night of Queen on Friday 9 October, Garou & Tayc on Saturday 10 October and Labess on Friday 30 October.

World.title: Mendoza Things to Do, 9 to 31 October 2026
World.content:
MENDOZA · Culture

Mendoza from 9 to 31 October 2026: the last days of the provincial book fair, Gabriel Rolón at Teatro Mendoza, free architecture tours and a Freud play on 31 October.

MENDOZA — This is the culture and events guide for expats, digital nomads and long-stay visitors who live in the city or nearby. It covers things to do in Mendoza from 9 to 31 October 2026, with venues, prices and ticket platforms.

The first weekend is the busiest. Friday 9 October brings evening shows in the city, and the book fair closes on Sunday 11 October. Monday 12 October is a national holiday, so the weekend runs for three days.

File photo: Plaza Independencia in Mendoza.

9 to 12 October: the long weekend

Friday 9 October, 15:00 Recorridos Arquitectónicos: Avenida Mitre and Calle Espejo Meeting area Av. Mitre and Calle Espejo, central Mendoza · Free, prior registration required The first of five free architecture walks starts at 15:00 with guide Graciela Moretti. The Municipal Museum of Modern Art (MMAMM) and the architecture faculty of the Universidad de Mendoza organise the series. Each walk lasts about two hours and takes 20 people, so register through the organisers’ online form before you go.

Friday 9 October, 21:00 Gabriel Rolón: Palabra Plena Teatro Mendoza, San Juan 1427 · Tickets via TuEntrada and EntradaWeb A theatre piece about language and what people say or leave unsaid.

Friday 9 October, 21:00 The Loota Music Band: Las canciones que nos salvaron Teatro Quintanilla, Espacio Cultural Plaza Independencia · EntradaWeb Live music and storytelling built around hits from the 1970s, 80s and 90s. The city’s press office says few seats remain. The narration gives context to the lyrics, which helps if you are still learning Spanish.

Sunday 11 October, 20:00 Liga Mendocina de Improvisación: 15th anniversary final Teatro Mendoza, San Juan 1427 · ARS 10,000 (about US$7) · EntradaWeb or the box office Four teams compete in the final: Joaco Mandril y sus Monos Capuchinos, Delirium Forte, Flor de Vikingos and Rebobine Por Favor. Audience votes and referees decide the winner. Improvised theatre in Spanish is fast and visual, so it is easier to follow than scripted drama.

Sunday 11 October Feria del Libro de Mendoza 2026: final day Espacio Cultural Julio Le Parc, Guaymallén The fair runs from 1 to 11 October and is dedicated to children’s and young-adult literature. Guests this year include Felipe Pigna and Eduardo Sacheri. Check the fair’s programme for the hours of the last day.

Monday 12 October, all day Día del Respeto a la Diversidad Cultural National public holiday The holiday falls on its original date, Monday 12 October, so it needs no move. Together with Saturday and Sunday it forms a three-day weekend. Plan errands and bank visits for before Friday 9 October evening or after Tuesday 13 October.

16 to 30 October: free architecture walks

The same MMAMM and Universidad de Mendoza series continues with four more walks. All are free, last about two hours and need advance registration, with 20 places each. The dates and meeting areas are below.

Friday 16 October, 10:00 Recorridos Arquitectónicos: Avenida Emilio Civit Av. Emilio Civit area, Mendoza · Free, registration required Guides Claudina Masini and Jimena Andía lead this walk along one of the city’s main avenues.

Friday 23 October, 11:00 Recorridos Arquitectónicos: Plaza Independencia Plaza Independencia, Mendoza · Free, registration required Guides Mercedes Castro, Mariano Arenas and Esteban Grimi lead the circuit around the central square.

Monday 26 October, 10:00 Recorridos Arquitectónicos: Plaza San Martín Plaza San Martín area, Mendoza · Free, registration required Guides Felipe Fiorentini and Verónica Cremaschi lead this walk through the surroundings of the square.

Friday 30 October, 10:00 Recorridos Arquitectónicos: Universidad de Mendoza Surroundings of the FAUD-UM architecture faculty · Free, registration required Guides Gabriel Bekerman and Alberto Lucchesi close the series around the faculty.

Saturday 31 October: Freud closes the month

Saturday 31 October, 21:00 La última sesión de Freud Cine Teatro Plaza, Godoy Cruz · Check the venue for tickets Luis Machín and Javier Lorenzo star in this play directed by Daniel Veronese. It imagines a duel of ideas between Sigmund Freud and the writer C.S. Lewis in London at the start of the Second World War.

Planning your Mendoza in October

Most of the shows above sell tickets through EntradaWeb, and Rolón’s show is also sold through TuEntrada. Prices in this guide are in Argentine pesos. We converted them at about ARS 1,516 per US dollar (RT market rate, 8 October 2026), and the US$ figures will move with the day’s rate.

Unsubscribe with one click in any edition. If you stop opening us for 30 days we stop sending by ourselves, as we assume the interest is no longer there. See our privacy policy. We never share your email.

Several venues sit outside the centre. Teatro Mendoza and Teatro Quintanilla are in the city, while Cine Teatro Plaza is in neighbouring Godoy Cruz. Check the route before you book a late show, and allow extra time to get home.

For weekly listings, follow the City of Mendoza press office and the venue ticket pages. Programmes change, so confirm start times on the ticket page on the day.

When is the Mendoza book fair in October 2026?

The Feria del Libro de Mendoza runs from 1 to 11 October at the Espacio Cultural Julio Le Parc and is dedicated to children’s and young-adult literature.

Is there a public holiday in Mendoza in October 2026?

Yes. Monday 12 October is the national holiday for the Día del Respeto a la Diversidad Cultural, which makes a three-day weekend.

Are there free events in Mendoza after 9 October 2026?

World.title: San Juan Events Guide for 9 to 31 October 2026
World.content:
SAN JUAN · Culture

San Juan from 9 to 31 October, day by day.

SAN JUAN — This guide is for people who live here, not weekend tourists. It lists the concerts, theatre and family shows worth crossing the city for between Friday 9 and Saturday 31 October 2026, arranged day by day. Every date, time and venue below was checked against the venue’s own calendar or the organiser’s announcement on 8 October.

The month starts with a heavy weekend of Latin pop, salsa and theatre. The Coliseo de Puerto Rico, the island’s largest indoor arena with room for 18,500 people, hosts a show almost every weekend. The Coca-Cola Music Hall in Distrito T-Mobile and the Centro de Bellas Artes in Santurce carry the rest.

Monday 12 October is Día de la Raza, the Puerto Rican name for Columbus Day, and holiday calendars list it as a public holiday. Banks and government offices normally close, so confirm with your employer or school. All prices are in US dollars, the island’s currency.

File photo: the Condado district and coast of San Juan.

9 to 11 October: Opening weekend

Friday 9 October Mon Laferte Coca-Cola Music Hall, Distrito T-Mobile · Tickets via Ticketera The Chilean singer-songwriter plays San Juan on her “Femme Fatale Tour”, presented by José Dueño. The venue lists the date and ticket link but not the start time, so confirm the door time with Ticketera before you plan dinner.

Friday 9 October, 8:00 p.m. A Chorus Line (final weekend) Centro de Bellas Artes Luis A. Ferré, Santurce · Tickets via Ticketera, Ticketcenter and the CBA box office The last performances are Friday 9 and Saturday 10 October at 8:00 p.m., and Sunday 11 October at 4:00 p.m. The musical won nine Tony Awards and the Pulitzer Prize. This production is in Spanish with an Puerto Rican cast, so English-only visitors will follow the story but not every line.

Saturday 10 October PJ Sin Suela Coca-Cola Music Hall, Distrito T-Mobile · Tickets via Ticketera The urban-music show is presented by No Limit Entertainment. The venue does not list a start time, so check it with Ticketera. The surrounding district has restaurants and bars, which makes it easy to build an evening around the concert.

Sunday 11 October, 8:00 p.m. Camilo: “Para cuando sean mayores” tour Coliseo de Puerto Rico, Hato Rey · Tickets via Ticketera The Colombian singer presents his fifth studio album, a record about time, family and fatherhood. The date moved from an earlier slot, so ignore older listings that show 2 October. The Coliseo requires children aged 15 or younger to be accompanied by an adult over 21.

16 to 18 October: Mid-month

Friday 16 October, 8:30 p.m. The Noise: La Última Noche Coliseo de Puerto Rico, Hato Rey · Tickets via Ticketera The show is billed as a farewell night that looks back at the roots and growth of reggaeton. The venue lists an 8:30 p.m. start. Expect a late finish and heavy traffic around Hato Rey afterwards.

Friday 16 October Rusowsky Coca-Cola Music Hall, Distrito T-Mobile · Tickets via Ticketera Rusowsky plays a José Dueño presentation. The venue lists the date but no start time, so confirm it before you travel.

Saturday 17 October, 8:30 p.m. Manny Manuel: “Rey de Corazones” Coliseo de Puerto Rico, Hato Rey · Tickets via Ticketera Manny Manuel brings his “Rey de Corazones” show to the arena. It is the second Coliseo concert in two nights after The Noise, so expect busy roads in Hato Rey.

Sunday 18 October, 6:00 p.m. Alex Zurdo: “Zona Zero” Coliseo de Puerto Rico, Hato Rey · Tickets via Ticketera The Puerto Rican Christian rapper and singer brings his “Zona Zero” show to the arena. The 6:00 p.m. start is early enough for families and for anyone who has work on Monday.

23 to 31 October: Late month

Friday 23 October, 8:30 p.m. Clarent Coliseo de Puerto Rico, Hato Rey · Tickets via Ticketera Clarent is a Puerto Rican singer and songwriter in Latin urban music.

Saturday 24 October, 8:30 p.m. Fiel a La Vega: 30 Años Coliseo de Puerto Rico, Hato Rey · From US$55 to US$125 The Puerto Rican rock band marks three decades since its 1996 debut album with a large production and special guests. Tickets went on sale on 29 May through Ticketera and the Coliseo box office. Songs such as “Salimos de Aquí” and “Bla, Bla, Bla” are expected. The venue lists 8:30 p.m., while the May press report gave 8:00 p.m., so arrive early.

Friday 30 October Bad Gyal: “Más Cara World Tour 2026” Coca-Cola Music Hall, Distrito T-Mobile · Tickets via Ticketera The Spanish reggaeton and dancehall artist stops in San Juan between Miami on 28 October and Chicago on 1 November. Time to be confirmed with the venue. Expect strong demand for a Friday before Halloween weekend.

Friday 30 October, 8:00 p.m., and Saturday 31 October, 1:00 p.m. and 7:00 p.m. Monster Jam 2026 Coliseo de Puerto Rico, Hato Rey · Tickets via Ticketera Monster trucks return to the Coliseo for three shows over Halloween weekend. It is the most family-friendly item on this list. The same under-15 and age-2 ticket rules apply as for other Coliseo events.

Planning your San Juan October

October is warm, humid and wet in San Juan. The National Weather Service has recorded Octobers as wet as 16.20 inches of rain (2010) and as dry as 1.95 inches (2011) since 1898. Plan an indoor backup for any evening.

The Atlantic hurricane season officially runs until 30 November. Check the National Weather Service forecast for San Juan before you travel to a night event, and keep your ticket confirmation on your phone.

Each venue has its own ticket rules. Coca-Cola Music Hall and Coliseo events sell through Ticketera, while the Centro de Bellas Artes also sells at its box office and through Ticketcenter. Buy from these official sellers, not from resale sites, to avoid fake tickets.

The Coliseo is at 500 Calle Arterial B in Hato Rey, and the Coca-Cola Music Hall is at 250 Convention Boulevard. Both get congested before and after big shows. Allow extra time, particularly on rainy nights, and consider a rideshare.

Frequently Asked Questions

What are the biggest concerts in San Juan in October 2026?

Mon Laferte plays the Coca-Cola Music Hall on Friday 9 October and Camilo plays the Coliseo de Puerto Rico on Sunday 11 October at 8:00 p.m. Fiel a La Vega plays the Coliseo on Saturday 24 October.

Is there a public holiday in Puerto Rico in October 2026?

Monday 12 October is Día de la Raza, known in the United States as Columbus Day, and holiday calendars list it as a public holiday in Puerto Rico. Banks and government offices usually close, so confirm with your employer or school.

Where can I buy tickets for San Juan events in October?

Coca-Cola Music Hall and Coliseo de Puerto Rico shows sell through Ticketera. A Chorus Line also sold through Ticketcenter and the Centro de Bellas Artes box office. Fiel a La Vega tickets also sell at the Coliseo box office.

What is the weather like in San Juan in October?

Expect warm, humid and wet weather. The National Weather Service has recorded Octobers with 16.20 inches of rain (2010) and with 1.95 inches (2011), and the Atlantic hurricane season lasts until 30 November.

Can I take children to the Coliseo de Puerto Rico?

Yes, but the Coliseo requires children aged 15 or younger to be accompanied by an adult over 21. Monster Jam on 30 and 31 October is the most family-oriented show of the month.

World.title: What to Do in Port Louis, 9 to 31 October 2026
World.content:
PORT LOUIS · Culture

The LA ISLA 2068 festival opens in Moka on Friday 9 October, and Caudan Arts Centre stages Feydeau theatre from Thursday 15 October. Here is the rest of the month, with prices in rupees and US$.

PORT LOUIS — This is the culture and events guide for 9 to 31 October 2026, for people who live in the capital or in nearby towns on the central plateau. Every date, time, venue and price below was checked on the organiser, venue or ticket-platform page on 8 October 2026.

Prices are in Mauritian rupees (Rs), each with its US$ value. We converted at the RT market rate of about Rs 47.4 per US$ (8 October 2026), so US$1 buys roughly Rs 47. Ticket platforms may add booking fees, and card providers add their own exchange spreads.

Port Louis itself hosts four theatre and concert productions at Caudan Arts Centre, on Marina Quay at Caudan Waterfront. Most other shows are in Moka, Trianon, Phoenix and on the west coast, so plan your transport early.

9 to 11 October: The opening weekend

Friday 9 October, 17:00 to 00:00, and Saturday 10 October, 12:00 to 00:00 LA ISLA 2068 Festival La Piazza, Vivéa Business Park, Moka · Saturday regular ticket Rs 1,600 (about US$34) · two-day Eco Pack (VIP) Rs 3,300 (about US$70) A two-day festival at the Vivéa Business Park in Moka. The Otayo listing showed the Friday regular and VIP tickets as sold out on 8 October, while Saturday regular tickets were still on sale at the “last chance” price. Children under 12 enter free, and visitors aged 12 to 25 get a 50% discount with a code listed on the ticket page. A valid ID must be shown at the door.

Saturday 10 October, 14:00 Lilo & Stitch – La Comédie Musicale Trianon Convention Centre, Trianon · from Rs 400 (about US$8) · all children aged 2 and over need a ticket A French-language family musical with performers travelling from Paris. The show lasts about 70 minutes, and doors open at 12:00. Premium tickets at Rs 1,200 (about US$25) include reserved parking.

Saturday 10 October, 17:00 La Reine des Neiges : La Comédie Musicale Trianon Convention Centre, Trianon · from Rs 400 (about US$8) · all children aged 2 and over need a ticket The second family musical of the day at Trianon. Doors open at 16:00, and Premium tickets (Rs 1,200, about US$25) include reserved parking.

Saturday 10 October, 20:00 Le Roi Lion – La Comédie Musicale Trianon Convention Centre, Trianon · from Rs 400 (about US$8) · all children aged 2 and over need a ticket The third musical in the Trianon series, with doors at 19:00. The five ticket categories run from Bronze at Rs 400 to Premium at Rs 1,200 (about US$25).

Saturday 10 October, 20:00 Elle sur île, Véronique Forget in concert Caudan Arts Centre, Caudan Waterfront, Port Louis · Rs 700 (about US$15) to Rs 1,200 (about US$25) A solo concert of known repertoire and new, unreleased songs, in English, French and Creole. It lasts about 1 hour 30 minutes.

Saturday 10 October, 18:00 to 00:00 Sam Garrett Live in Concert The Green Village, southern Mauritius · adults Rs 1,800 (about US$38) · children 7 to 12 Rs 900 (about US$19) A family-friendly concert in the south of the island. Children under 6 enter free, and VIP adult tickets cost Rs 2,500 (about US$53). It is a long drive from Port Louis, so arrange the return journey in advance.

Saturday 10 October, 19:30, and Sunday 11 October, 16:30 Christafari – Reggae Revival Mauritius J&J Auditorium, Phoenix · Rs 450 (about US$10) per ticket A reggae concert on two dates, one on Saturday evening and one on Sunday afternoon. Children aged 3 and over need a ticket, and younger children must sit on a parent’s lap. Otayo listed the Sunday show as having last tickets available.

15 to 18 October: Theatre and a classical concert in the capital

Thursday 15, Friday 16 and Saturday 17 October, 19:30 Tailleur pour Dames Caudan Arts Centre, Caudan Waterfront, Port Louis · Standard Rs 750 (about US$16) · VIP Rs 950 (about US$20) A vaudeville comedy by Georges Feydeau, performed in French by a cast of eight. In the story, a respected doctor is trapped by his own lies and must pose as a dressmaker. The play lasts 1 hour 45 minutes and was Feydeau’s first three-act play, written when he was 23.

Friday 16 October, 22:30 NOCHE Latina Lakaz Cascavelle, Cascavelle · Rs 500 (about US$11) presale · 18+ only A night of reggaeton, Latin and Kizomba music with about 15 local artists in showcases, and DJs Moon Jr and Kidz between acts. Tickets are limited and cost more at the door. Outside food and drink are not allowed, and security checks may take place at entry.

Saturday 17 October, 12:00 to 20:00 Espresso & Beats – Brew to Bubbles La Rivière Tamarin, Tamarin · entrance Rs 500 (about US$11) · entrance with lunch Rs 2,500 (about US$53) A daytime event that moves from coffee to cocktails to sparkling wine at sunset. Four DJs play house and Afro house with a live saxophonist. The lunch ticket includes a three-course menu.

Saturday 17 October, 20:00 JARRY – BONHOMME Trianon Convention Centre, Trianon · from Rs 900 (about US$19) · VIP Rs 2,800 (about US$59) A comedy show in French that lasts about 1 hour 30 minutes. Other categories cost Rs 1,200 (about US$25) and Rs 1,800 (about US$38). Children aged 3 and over need a ticket.

Sunday 18 October, 17:00 Grand Concert Performing European Composers Caudan Arts Centre, Caudan Waterfront, Port Louis · Rs 700 (about US$15) to Rs 1,200 (about US$25) A classical concert of 1 hour 15 minutes, organised by Immedia with the European Union. The first half is the final of a competition for young Mauritian musicians, with a choir from the national music conservatory between the halves. In the second half, Kenneth Babajie performs with an ensemble. Children under 12 pay Rs 700 (about US$15).

22 to 25 October: A Mauritian stage production

Thursday 22, Friday 23 and Saturday 24 October, 20:00; Sunday 25 October, 14:00 Les Enfants d’Un Rêve : Pa Per Revé Caudan Arts Centre, Caudan Waterfront, Port Louis · Rs 700 (about US$15) A musical show for the 25th anniversary of a volunteer group that has performed since 2001, backed by the band Les Firehawks. It is performed in French, English and Creole and lasts about 2 hours 30 minutes. The show raises money for a local charity.

30 and 31 October: Reggae nights and a comedy finale

Friday 30 October, 19:30 to 01:00 VIBE DANS BACKSTAGE Backstage, Hennessy Park Hotel, Ébène · Rs 450 (about US$10) early bird · 18+ only A night of reggae, seggae and ragga with live sets by Sayaa and Blakkayo, a showcase by Sebby and DJ sets by Adellio. It starts after the working day and ends at 01:00.

Saturday 31 October, 20:00 Booder… à l’école Trianon Convention Centre, Trianon · Bronze Rs 750 (about US$16) · VIP Rs 1,500 (about US$32) A French comedy show by Booder with seated tickets in five categories. The top VVIP ticket costs Rs 1,800 (about US$38) and includes reserved parking. Children aged 3 and over need a ticket.

Presale tickets are cheaper than door prices.

World.title: Why Higher Oil Prices Rattle Asian Stocks
World.content:
ASIA · ANALYSIS

Key Facts — What is happening Asian stocks fell on 8 October 2026: Japan’s Nikkei 225 lost 1.4%, South Korea’s Kospi 2.6% and China’s Shanghai Composite 0.8%, while US crude rose.

— Why it matters Japan, South Korea, India and China buy most of their oil abroad, so dearer crude lifts costs and squeezes company profits.

— The numbers US crude (WTI) rose about 3.5% to roughly US$91.4 a barrel in US trading, and the 10-year US Treasury yield stood at 5.23%.

— Who is who Brazil and Colombia are net oil exporters in Latin America; Mexico exports crude but imports refined fuel.

— Prediction markets Polymarket prices a 62.5% chance that WTI touches US$95 in October and 35% for US$100 (US$1.33 million traded; read 5:17 pm ET, 8 October 2026).

— What it means for you US holders of Asian ETFs and ADRs face higher energy costs and high US yields at once; Petrobras and Ecopetrol shares rose on the day.

Asian stock markets fell on 8 October 2026 as oil prices rose again, with the Nikkei 225 down 1.4%, the Kospi down 2.6% and the Shanghai Composite down 0.8%. For US readers the link is direct: American portfolios hold Asian ETFs and ADRs, and the same oil move lifts producers in Latin America.

Asia imports most of the oil it burns. When crude rises, the bill lands on households, airlines, chemical makers and governments within weeks. This analysis explains how that works, who is most exposed, and why Brazil and Colombia sit on the other side of the trade.

What Happened on 8 October

Japan’s Nikkei 225 fell 1.4% to 69,042, and South Korea’s Kospi fell 2.6% to 6,626, the biggest drop of the major Asian indices (RT market data). The Shanghai Composite slipped 0.8% to 3,811.90, and Hong Kong’s Hang Seng also lost more than 1%.

Oil moved the other way. In US trading, West Texas Intermediate (WTI), the US benchmark, rose about 3.5% to roughly US$91.4 a barrel, according to the Bloomberg market wrap carried by Swissinfo. The US Oil Fund (USO), an exchange-traded fund that tracks WTI futures, gained 2.6% on RT data.

Oil has swung sharply since the summer. The Associated Press reported on 11 September that crude was moving on whether the United States and Iran could agree to let tankers leave the Persian Gulf freely again.

The Kospi fell 2.6% to 6,626 on 8 October 2026. Chart: The Rio Times, RT data.

Nikkei 225 closed at 69,042 on 8 October 2026, down 1.4% on the day. Chart: The Rio Times, RT data.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Why Oil Hurts Asian Equities

The first reason is trade. Japan and South Korea have almost no domestic crude, and India and China depend heavily on imports too. A dearer barrel widens their import bills and weighs on their currencies. The yen traded near 157.9 per US dollar on 8 October, so oil priced in dollars costs Japanese buyers even more.

The second reason is costs. Fuel feeds into transport, plastics, fertiliser and food. Airlines, shipping lines, refiners and petrochemical producers feel it first. If firms pass the cost on, headline inflation rises, and central banks have less room to cut interest rates.

The third reason is US interest rates. The 10-year US Treasury yield was 5.23% on 8 October, according to the same Bloomberg wrap, which also reported that Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller expects more rate hikes. High US yields make dollar bonds more attractive than Asian stocks, and they lower the value of future profits, which hits technology shares hardest. Chip stocks fell more than 3% in US trading on the day, and the Kospi and Nikkei both lean heavily on chip makers.

Who Is Most Exposed

South Korea and Japan combine heavy oil imports with large technology sectors, so they face both the cost shock and the rate shock. That helps explain the Kospi’s larger fall. India is another large importer, and its Sensex fell about 1.5% during Thursday’s session on RT data. China imports a great deal too, but its domestic market is driven more by local demand and policy, and its fall was smaller.

Not every Asian company loses. Oil producers and some state-owned energy groups can gain when prices rise. But stock indices are dominated by banks, manufacturers, consumer firms and technology companies, so the broad index usually falls when oil jumps.

Latin America on the Other Side

Higher crude moves income toward exporters. Brazil’s Petrobras, listed in New York as PBR, rose 2.9% to US$24.69 on 8 October. Colombia’s Ecopetrol (EC) rose 1.9% to US$16.95 (RT, closing data).

Brazil and Colombia both produce more crude than they use, so a higher price raises export income and government revenue. The gain is not automatic. Brazil can hold down domestic fuel prices, which limits what Petrobras earns at home. Mexico also exports crude, but it imports much of its gasoline and diesel, so its benefit is smaller.

What Prediction Markets Say

On Polymarket, traders put a 62.5% probability on WTI touching US$95 at some point in October 2026 and 35% on US$100. They put 94.5% on a dip to US$90, and 59.5% on a dip to US$85. More than US$1.3 million has been traded on this market. Prices are as of 5:17 pm ET on 8 October 2026.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What It Means for You

If you own a Japan, South Korea, India or broad Asia-Pacific fund, expect oil to be one of its swing factors while the Gulf stays unsettled. The same oil move can help Latin American energy shares in your portfolio. Check how much of a fund sits in technology and in energy importers before drawing conclusions from one day of trading.

What Is Not Known

Reports point to several drivers for the oil rise on 8 October, including the US–Iran standoff, and none is confirmed as the sole cause. Nor is it clear whether the move will last, or whether it will feed into core inflation in Asia. How far the Fed will raise rates is also open; Governor Waller’s expectation is one view, not a decision.

What to Watch

The next US consumer price report is due on Wednesday 14 October 2026 at 8:30 am ET (12:30 UTC). A hot reading would add pressure on bond yields and on Asian shares. Weekly US crude inventory data follow on Thursday 15 October. Watch also the yen near 158 per dollar, and any news on tanker passage through the Persian Gulf.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why do higher oil prices hit Asian stock markets?

Most large Asian economies import most of their crude, so dearer oil raises transport, factory and food costs and weakens trade balances. It can also keep US interest rates high, which lowers the value of future profits and weighs on shares.

Which Asian markets fell on 8 October 2026?

The Nikkei 225 fell 1.4% to 69,042, the Kospi 2.6% to 6,626 and the Shanghai Composite 0.8% to 3,811.90, according to RT market data.

How much did oil rise on 8 October 2026?

West Texas Intermediate rose about 3.5% to roughly US$91.4 a barrel in US trading, according to the Bloomberg market wrap carried by Swissinfo.

Which Latin American companies gain from higher oil prices?

Producers such as Brazil’s Petrobras and Colombia’s Ecopetrol benefit from higher crude. Their New York-listed shares rose 2.9% and 1.9% on 8 October 2026.

What are prediction markets saying about oil?

On Polymarket, traders gave a 62.5% chance that WTI touches US$95 in October 2026 and 35% for US$100, as of 5:17 pm ET on 8 October. These are bets, not forecasts by officials.

World.title: Chile Mudslide Sweeps Cars Through Las Condes
World.content:
A flash flood of mud, rocks and logs, known in Spanish as an aluvión, swept vehicles through the San Carlos de Apoquindo sector of Las Condes in Santiago, Chile, on Thursday 8 October 2026. Las Condes is an eastern commune of the capital so the event matters to US travellers, expats and companies with staff in the city.

Intense rain over a short period activated a ravine, called a quebrada, near the Andes, according to Chilean outlets. Carabineros, Chile’s national police, reported high water flow on General Blanche at 5:00 pm local time.

Video shows several vehicles carried away by the mud, including a RED bus, part of Santiago’s public transport network, with passengers aboard. The early reports we reviewed mentioned no injuries or deaths, and readers in the US with plans in Santiago should check official travel advice.

Key Facts —Who. Senapred (Chile’s national disaster agency), the Presidential Delegation of the Metropolitan region and the Las Condes municipality are responding. —What. An aluvión, a flash flood of mud and debris, set off by intense rain and an activated ravine. —Where. San Carlos de Apoquindo, Las Condes, Santiago, near the Andes. —When. Late afternoon on Thursday 8 October 2026, about 5 pm Chile time. —Status. As of 8 October 2026, 21:20 GMT

What We Know

The rain activated a ravine, and La Tercera reported a canal overflow on Francisco Bulnes Correa street. Emol and Diario Financiero list affected streets including General Blanche, Quebrada Honda, Avenida La Plaza, Camino El Alba, Paul Harris, Cristóbal Colón and Álvaro del Portillo.

File photo: Parque Almagro Metro station in Santiago. The image does not show the flooded area.

Miguel Muñoz, the Metropolitan regional director of Senapred, said the intense precipitation had produced a flash flood in Las Condes. Authorities urged residents to follow evacuation directives issued through official channels, La Tercera reported.

Germán Codina, the Presidential Delegate for the Metropolitan region, said authorities were evaluating an emergency SMS alert, known as SAE, with evacuation recommendations. Diario Financiero reported that Codina requested Public Works Ministry machinery and that the perimeter runs between Camino El Alba, Vital Apoquindo and the cordillera to the east.

Clínica UC San Carlos de Apoquindo was reported flooded, and Universidad de Los Andes restricted entry, exit and vehicle removal for staff and students. The Las Condes municipality advised residents to avoid the affected sectors.

A similar mudflow hit the same area on 31 January 2026. La Tercera reported that it dragged sediments, rocks and logs through Francisco Bulnes Correa, and Mayor Catalina San Martín said 11 homes were flooded.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

What Is Not Known

The exact number of vehicles swept away is not known, and the reports we reviewed do not give a full count. Rainfall totals and the extent of the damage to homes, roads and businesses were also not given.

It is also unclear whether evacuations are complete, or how long the affected streets will stay closed. No injuries or deaths had been reported in the early reports we reviewed, but the situation was still developing.

What It Means for Travelers and US Readers

Anyone in Santiago should follow the instructions of Senapred and the Las Condes municipality, including evacuation orders. Avoid ravine areas and the streets named above while crews work.

Travellers and expats should check their government’s official travel advice, and ask their hotel or employer, before moving around eastern Santiago. The Las Condes municipality has asked residents to avoid the affected sectors.

US companies with staff in Las Condes may wish to confirm that colleagues are safe and know the local instructions. The January mudflow in the same area shows that the sector has faced this hazard before.

For wider context, see our Latin America coverage and our guide to the best places to live in Chile for expats. We will add confirmed details as official sources publish them.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is an aluvión?

An aluvión is a flash flood of mud and debris, often carrying rocks and logs. In Las Condes it followed intense rain over a short period.

Were people hurt in the Las Condes flood?

No injuries or deaths had been reported in the early reports we reviewed. Rainfall totals, damage and evacuation progress were not yet known.

What should travellers in Santiago do?

Follow the instructions of Senapred and the Las Condes municipality, and avoid ravine areas. Check official travel advice and stay out of affected areas, as the Las Condes municipality advised.

Has this happened in Las Condes before?

A similar mudflow hit the same area on 31 January 2026, La Tercera reported. Mayor Catalina San Martín said then that 11 homes were flooded.

World.title: Brazil Orders Eduardo Bolsonaro to Prison
World.content:
Key Facts —Who. Eduardo Bolsonaro, a former federal deputy and son of Jair Bolsonaro. He says he is politically persecuted. —What. Justice Alexandre de Moraes ordered his prison sentence to start, with an arrest warrant and cancelled Brazilian passports. The sentence is 4 years and 2 months, initially in a semi-open regime. —Where. The order comes from Brazil’s Supreme Court in Brasília. He lives in the United States and holds a green card. —When. The decision was reported on Thursday 8 October 2026. The conviction was on Tuesday 16 June 2026. —Status. As of 8 October 2026, 20:30 GMT

Brazil’s Supreme Court has ordered Eduardo Bolsonaro, son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, to start his prison sentence, in a decision reported on Thursday 8 October 2026. He has lived in the United States since early 2025, and his conviction rests on lobbying American officials for tariffs and sanctions on Brazil.

What We Know

Moraes ordered the start of the sentence, an arrest warrant and the cancellation of all Brazilian passports issued to Eduardo Bolsonaro. The conviction became final on 3 October 2026, according to Brazilian media reports.

The order also enters him in the National Imprisonment Monitoring Bank (BNMP) and issues a detention guide, as reported. His political rights are suspended during the sentence.

The court sentenced him to 4 years and 2 months, initially in a semi-open regime, for coercion in the course of legal proceedings. The sentence follows the ruling of the First Panel in June.

He must also pay 50 day-fines of two minimum wages each, roughly R$160,000 (about US$32,000). We use the EODHD rate of R$5.02 per US$ on 8 October.

He is barred from running for office until eight years after he serves the sentence. The panel also ordered the loss of his Federal Police post in June.

Brazil’s National Congress in Brasília, where Eduardo Bolsonaro served as a federal deputy. (File photo)

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Eduardo Bolsonaro (Brazil) Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

How the Conviction Came About

The First Panel of the Supreme Court convicted him unanimously on Tuesday 16 June 2026. The votes came from Moraes, Flávio Dino, Cármen Lúcia and Cristiano Zanin.

The panel found he used his position as a deputy to seek help from US authorities to pressure justices. It said he tried to interfere in the coup trial that convicted his father, Jair Bolsonaro, of attempted coup.

The court pointed to his push for US tariffs on Brazilian exports as concrete harm. Prosecutors had separately said US visas were revoked for 8 of the 11 Supreme Court justices.

The court rejected his appeal, known as embargos de declaração, unanimously on Friday 18 September 2026. That appeal challenged the June conviction.

The appeal came from the Federal Public Defender’s Office. Eduardo Bolsonaro says he is politically persecuted and that he was never validly notified of the case.

What Is Not Known

Moraes sent the warrant to the Federal Police, but Eduardo Bolsonaro is abroad. No extradition request has been reported, and it is not known whether Brazil will file one.

It is unclear whether the US will act on the order. No reaction from the US government appears in the sources we reviewed.

We do not know how Eduardo Bolsonaro will respond, or whether he will return to Brazil voluntarily. Brazilian media report that a green card makes extradition harder, which is their assessment.

What It Means for US Readers

Eduardo Bolsonaro has lived in the United States since early 2025 and received a US green card in July 2026, as our earlier coverage of the green card row explains. The case against him rests on his lobbying of US officials, which ties the ruling directly to American policy toward Brazil.

The conviction cites his push for US tariffs on Brazilian goods. How Washington treats a convicted person who holds a green card is not yet known.

We have also reported that he was dismissed from the Federal Police. Argentina’s Javier Milei was due to join him at a gala in Washington on 14 October, and his attendance after the order is not confirmed.

The next step to watch is whether Brazil files an extradition request. More news is in our Brazil coverage.

Background: Brazil Tax Reform 2026 Replaces Five Taxes With Two VATs.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why was Eduardo Bolsonaro sentenced?

The First Panel of the Supreme Court found he used his position as a deputy to seek help from US authorities to pressure justices. It ruled that he tried to interfere in the coup trial of his father, Jair Bolsonaro.

How long is the Eduardo Bolsonaro prison sentence?

The sentence is 4 years and 2 months, initially in a semi-open regime, for coercion in the course of legal proceedings. He also faces a fine of roughly US$32,000 and is barred from office until eight years after he serves it.

Where is Eduardo Bolsonaro now?

He has lived in the United States since early 2025 and received a US green card in July 2026. Moraes sent the arrest warrant to the Federal Police, but he is abroad.

Can Eduardo Bolsonaro be extradited from the US?

Brazilian media report that a green card makes extradition harder, which is their assessment. No extradition request has been reported in the sources we reviewed.
