World.title: Croatian Protest Against Rising Taxes and Levies Announced
World.content:
October the 7th, 2026 – Another Croatian protest has been announced against rising taxes, levies and costs on the 10th of October in Zagreb.

The association Glas poduzetnika (Voice of Entrepreneurs) and the association Spasimo male obiteljske iznajmljivače (Save Small Family Renters) are organising the protest “Enough of the levies” on Saturday, the 10th of October, at 12:00 on Zagreb’s Zrinjevac. As Index, they want to protest to warn about the rising costs of living and doing business and to demand a lower tax burden, more responsible spending of public money and safer working conditions.

taxes and the real cost of wages

Dario Kožul, member of the Management Board of UGP, pointed out that the amount a worker receives in their account represents only part of the total cost of their wage. A significant portion goes to taxes and contributions, and the worker additionally pays VAT when spending their net wage on products and services. “The worker sees how much has been deposited into their account, but that is not everything the employer paid for their work. When they spend that money, they pay tax again. That is why we must talk about how much people have left for living, how much the state takes and what we get for that money,” Kožul said.

relief proposals

UGP Management Board member Kristina Bakula presented a series of concrete demands. She called for the abolition of the so-called anchor prices and the mandatory daily publication of price lists on the internet, as well as amendments to the Consumer Protection Act in the part that regulates base prices. She stressed that a serious discussion about prices must include taxes, VAT, labour costs and energy. “The price will not fall because it is published in one more place. Costs and VAT need to be reduced. If the Government is increasing the minimum wage, at the same time it should increase the non-taxable part of income and relieve the burden on labour. The simplest test of every measure is: how much more did the worker get, and how much did the state? The answer must be — more for the worker,” Bakula said.

Among the demands is also a reduction of contributions for lower income brackets and the abandonment of additional taxation of higher ones. Bakula supported the introduction of voluntary membership in chambers and tourist boards, as well as the application of the principle of warning and correction before punishment for minor omissions that can be corrected immediately. “If an organisation is worth something, people will want to stay in it. If the law has to keep them, maybe the problem is not with the members but with the organisation. And for a minor omission the state’s first reaction should be to correct the error, because a mistake is not fraud,” she said. She also emphasised the state’s obligation to respect its own decisions and protect existing permits and categorisations, which is particularly important for family renters. She believes that citizens who have invested according to the permits obtained must have clear and predictable conditions and protection of acquired rights.

attitudes towards business owners

She also commented on the way representatives of the authorities communicate with citizens and entrepreneurs. “The minister is there to talk to people, listen to them and offer solutions. He is the minister of all citizens who fill the budget from which his function is paid. The ministry is not a private lodge, and citizens are not extras in the minister’s film. We expect him to solve problems and to discuss people’s existence seriously, responsibly and with arguments,” Bakula emphasised.

UGP President Bruno Samardžić added that the discussion about price increases must also deal with the state’s decisions. He explained that taxes, levies and administrative obligations affect business costs, and their burden can spill over onto citizens through higher prices and less room for wage growth.“If you’re asking all of us to tighten our belts, show where you have tightened yours. Before new burdens, review your own costs, political employment and the accumulation of administration. I call on everyone to deal with the real problems: productivity and competitiveness, and not to keep going round in circles chasing our own tail. For entrepreneurs this Saturday is not just a struggle, but also an opportunity for their voice to finally be heard,” Samardžić said.

The organisers demand that for every new administrative obligation at least two existing ones be abolished. They also demand that tax changes and new levies must go through public consultation instead of being adopted under urgent procedure, and that regulations be drafted in cooperation with those to whom they apply. They rejected claims that political parties are behind the protest and emphasised that the gathering is organised independently, motivated by the problems of their members. “We have nothing against political support from all sides. Anyone who supports our demands is welcome. But no one stands behind us except ourselves. We determine our own demands, make decisions and organise the protest,” Samardžić stressed. Entrepreneurs, craftsmen, renters, workers, pensioners, students and all citizens who, as they state, want more money for living and more responsible management of public money have been invited to the protest.

World.title: Defense agency launches €195M tender for arms and ammunition
World.content:
The Estonian Center for Defense Investments (RKIK) has launched a tender for weapons, ammunition, components and training with an estimated value of up to €195 million.

The procurement is split into five lots — three for ammunition worth €145 million and two for weapons worth €50 million — with seven-year framework agreements for each.

The sum makes it among the larger defense procurements the RKIK has issued to date.

Under the terms of the tender, the RKIK intends to conclude a framework agreement to purchase 40 mm and 23 mm weaponry plus 76 mm, 40 mm and 23 mm ammunition. The tender also covers the purchase of various types of these weapons and ammunition and their components, along with training and instruction, as well as life-cycle support services.

The ammunition types include blank rounds, training and practice ammunition, as well as a range of live ammunition with various lethal and non-lethal projectiles.

The products must be manufactured in EU or NATO member states and currently be in use as standard equipment by conventional military units or special forces in EU or NATO countries. Products currently being introduced into service in these countries are also eligible.

The RKIK will conclude framework agreements with a maximum estimated total value of €195 million.

Under the draft contract, the seller may, in justified cases, request an advance payment of up to 30 percent of the contract value, but RKIK retains the right to refuse the advance payment.

If an advance payment has been made but the seller fails to fulfill its obligations, it must immediately refund the advance payment, including VAT, to the buyer.

The RKIK is accepting tender bids until November 13 this year.

Estonia's largest defense contract so far remains the €400 million IRIS-T SLM air defense system, signed jointly with Latvia in 2023. A HIMARS deal in 2022, worth over $200 million, was described at the time as the largest weapons procurement in Estonia up to that point.

World.title: Rally Estonia put on WRC calendar also for next season
World.content:
FIA and the WRC promoter unveiled the calendar for next season's World Rally Championship on Thursday, with Rally Estonia also included. The event will take place on the roads of southern Estonia from July 22-25.

In August this year, the FIA World Rally Championship's promoter changed hands, with French automotive technology company Cosmobilis and private equity investor Park Square Capital acquiring WRC Promoter GmbH. The new owners aim to make the championship and its individual rounds even more attractive, turning each rally into a major event offering a wide range of entertainment alongside exciting racing.

The championship's new CEO, Eric Boullier, also visited Delfi Rally Estonia this summer and was highly impressed by what he saw. He praised the high standard of organization and the organizers' ambition and ability to combine world-class rallying with a comprehensive sports and entertainment experience.

Following this year's rally, the Rally Estonia team held several further meetings with representatives of the promoter. These discussions resulted in an agreement for Rally Estonia to remain a round of the World Rally Championship in 2027.

"Rally Estonia's continued inclusion in the WRC calendar is a major recognition of everyone who has contributed to the event's success. A big thank you to the Estonian state, local governments, private sector sponsors and the entire organizing team and of course to local residents, rally fans, drivers and teams," rally director Urmo Aava said.

"WRC Delfi Rally Estonia is much more than four days of top-level racing. It is a major international event that boosts Estonia's economy, supports regional development, generates tax revenue for the state and provides memorable experiences for tens of thousands of spectators along the stages and hundreds of millions of viewers across various platforms. The desire of foreign visitors to return to Estonia and recommend us to their friends creates value long after the rally weekend has ended," Minister of Culture Heidy Purga added.

WRC Rally Estonia will be the ninth round of the 2027 FIA World Rally Championship, taking place from July 22–25. The 2027 WRC calendar will feature a total of 15 rounds.

The WRC is set to become even more global in the coming years, with the United States also hosting a championship round in 2027. The series will also enter a new era with the introduction of new Rally1 cars and technical regulations. Several new private teams are expected to join the championship, while Ford recently announced that it would return as a factory team after a decades-long absence. These developments promise to make the championship even more exciting and competitive.

Of the 43,894 unique spectators who attended this year's WRC Delfi Rally Estonia, foreign visitors accounted for 31.9 percent or 14,002 people. According to a study, the event generated an estimated €44.9 million in additional revenue for Estonian businesses, up 36 percent from 2025. Direct tax revenue associated with this turnover was estimated at €8.3 million.

World.title: Gold coins seized at Estonian-Russian border put up for auction
World.content:
Nearly €400,000 worth of gold coins found hidden in a truck seat at Estonia's Luhamaa border checkpoint are now up for grabs after authorities put them up for auction.

The Estonian Tax and Customs Board (MTA) is auctioning 157 gold coins, valued at about €390,000, that were seized at the southeastern border crossing last year.

Customs officers found the coins, weighing nearly 4.8 kilograms, hidden inside a truck seat on August 8 as they inspected the vehicle before it left Estonia.

A criminal investigation was opened over an alleged attempted sanctions violation and to determine who owned the coins. After the owner could not be identified, a court ordered the coins forfeited to the state.

The coins are being auctioned in small lots through Osta.ee, a local online auction site similar to eBay. Bidding on the first eight coins runs through October 14.

World.title: Estonian Spa Association: There may not be enough customers for all new spas
World.content:
Several new spas are set to enter Estonia's market in the coming years, but Aire Toffer, CEO of the Estonian Spa Association, warns that there may not be enough solvent customers to fill both the new and existing facilities.

Toffer said that the completion of several new spas is planned for the end of next year and the beginning of 2028. In her view, an incorrect impression may have formed about the spa market, as if large amounts of money were circulating there.

"These perceptions have arisen from the fact that during school holidays and on Saturday evenings the prices in spas are very high," she explained. Toffer said these are isolated days when visitors have time to go to the spa, which makes it possible to charge higher prices.

She said that starting spa entrepreneurs may lack an understanding of what the cost side of spas looks like, such as electricity and water consumption. "It's worth looking at companies' financial reports — the accommodation sector is not a very profitable business," Toffer noted.

Still, she is optimistic that every product has a consumer if it is created in the right place and is distinctive and innovative. But at present, according to Toffer, Estonia does not have enough solvent customers to fill all spas.

Spa center (photo is illustrative). Source: Anna Aurelia Minev/ERR

Gross: if you do it well, there should be enough customers

Next year, a spa hotel will rise by Lake Viljandi, owned by Lääne‑Virumaa entrepreneur Oleg Gross. He said that if you do something, you must do it very well. "And if you do it very well, there should be enough customers," he added.

Gross noted that a spa must offer a premium‑class product. "Besides, life has shown that Estonians have started going to spas more," he said. Gross explained that although foreign tourism has decreased, Estonia's climate encourages Estonians to visit spas more. He stated that a spa hotel is not a profit project but rather an emotion project. "But that it would start running losses — I don't believe that," he said.

According to Gross, there is room on the spa market for one more spa. At the same time, he noted that many developers have built a hotel with a spa only with bank loans and have no other business. "But we have a parent company in food retail," he said.

Oleg Gross Autor/allikas: ERR

Gross said that if the spa should run a slight loss in its early years, he does not plan to sell or close it, and the spa will be kept alive by force if necessary. "It will get going in any case, there is no doubt about that," he noted.

According to Toffer, whether every spa will have enough guests does not depend solely on Estonian visitors. "Many other things also play a role here — for example, how accessible Estonia is, whether we have flight connections, what will happen with airBaltic," she explained. Toffer stated that when designing a tourism service, foreign visitors are always considered as well.

Foreign visitors are also needed

"Certainly, we also need to do something at the national level to find visitors from other target markets outside Estonia who would come to Estonia because of the spas," she said. Toffer explained that this requires better marketing messages and promoting Estonia even more as a health‑oriented country.

While it is often visible how various companies close their doors because customers do not have the money to visit them, this is not seen much with spas. "Perhaps spa entrepreneurs have been more patient and have become accustomed to the fact that this is not a very profitable business," Toffer suggested.

She explained that in the current economy most entrepreneurs are trying to make ends meet, and if many more spas are added, it is not excluded that someone may have to close their doors.

"Entrepreneurs have a very high tax burden, and our VAT is unreasonably high compared to neighboring competitor countries," Toffer said. She added that if someone decides to end their activity in the current economic environment, they cannot be blamed for it.

World.title: Estonia's military conscription no-show rate falls to 2%
World.content:
The number of young adults failing to report for conscript service in the Estonian Defense Forces (EDF) has fallen steadily in recent years, reaching 2 percent in 2025.

A total of 63 call-up selectees failed to report for conscription last year, down from 4 percent in 2024 and 6.6 percent in 2023, the Defense Resources Agency (KRA) said.

KRA Conscripts Office director Krista Juhanson told ERR that those who repeatedly skip required medical assessments without good reason can be subject to official orders and an enforcement fine.

She said fines for failing to attend a medical assessment, which are intended to encourage compliance, are currently capped at €640, with the exact amount depending on the circumstances. Next year, however, the cap will double to €1,280.

"It's important to note that paying the fine does not exempt you from having to attend the medical assessment," Juhanson said.

KRA can impose fines repeatedly, but if that proves ineffective, the agency can seek to suspend a selectee's driver's license or fishing, hunting and firearms permits.

So far this year, the KRA has sought the suspension of 57 driver's licenses. Juhanson said that in practice, these extra measures generally work.

"Once call-up selectees grasp that failing to fulfill their obligations can result in additional consequences, they usually come in for the medical assessment," she said, adding that the goal is to encourage compliance, not punitive.

More flexible medicals

The KRA official also attributed the decline in no-shows in part to a more flexible approach, including a digital pre-assessment review of health records and allowing call-up selectees to choose when and where to have their assessment done.

"That means no more having to spend all day waiting your turn outside a doctor's office," Juhanson said.

Being summoned to a medical assessment doesn't automatically result in a conscription order either, she added, as when and where a selectee will be sent for conscript service are decided only after the assessment.

World.title: Solar parks driving electricity price down but could result in higher transmission charges
World.content:
Sunny summers are bringing zero and negative prices to the electricity market with increasing frequency, raising questions for renewable energy developers about how they can recoup their investments.

Southern Estonia's largest solar park has begun operating at the former Raadi military airfield. With a capacity of 74 megawatts, the park could theoretically meet half the electricity needs of Tartu's households. However, summer sunshine and falling electricity prices pose a significant profitability risk for the producer.

"With projects like these, you certainly have to think very carefully about when to generate electricity, when to sell it and when to store it. There will certainly be quite a few instances when production has to be curtailed," said Kristo Seli, CEO of Estiko Group.

According to researchers, Estonia's electricity grid faces a paradox: While summer production drives down wholesale electricity prices, connecting additional power plants to the grid brings new costs for consumers.

"When we add power plants or solar parks and they generate more energy, that should bring electricity prices down. At the same time, additional equipment is being added to the grid, making it more complex, and that could lead to higher network fees," said Ivo Palu, a professor at Tallinn University of Technology's (TalTech) Department of Electrical Power Engineering and Mechatronics.

The main problem is the mismatch between when electricity is generated and when it is consumed.

"We can't take the sunshine from Midsummer Day and bring it with us to Christmas. That would require different kinds of solutions," said Toomas Plank, director of the University of Tartu's Institute of Physics.

Although energy storage is increasingly needed to balance the grid, the government does not plan to impose mandatory requirements on developers, instead leaving it to market prices to drive investment.

"It also makes much more economic sense to build hybrid parks. When the sun is shining, you can generate cheap electricity from solar panels, store it and then sell it on the market when prices peak. Both the developer and, in the long run, the consumer benefit, with consumers getting lower electricity prices," said Minister of Energy and the Environment Erkki Keldo.

Estiko plans to build a large-scale battery storage facility at Raadi by the middle of next summer. The Raadi project thus demonstrates that the future of solar energy lies in hybrid solutions that help keep electricity prices reasonable even when the sun is not shining.

World.title: Dmitri Teperik: Ida-Viru County should be pro-Estonian, European and successful
World.content:
Ida-Viru County must be seen not as a region defined by its problems, but as a source of opportunity for Estonia's future, with long-term investment, local involvement and development essential to the country's prosperity and security, Dmitri Teperik writes.

"I'm from Ida-Viru County." I believe the emotional and substantive meaning of this sentence has changed more over the years than any statistical indicator collected about the county. I remember a time when it was met with a sympathetic nod. I also remember a time when it was followed by a cautious pause. At the same time, I sincerely hope that, before long, it will simply spark curiosity or, better yet, genuine enthusiasm.

I have spent most of my professional life working on security and societal resilience in Estonia, Ukraine and elsewhere. The longer I do this work, the clearer one thing becomes: The most important decisions, those with the longest-lasting impact, are not made in the midst of a sudden crisis. They are made years earlier, on ordinary workdays when passionate election promises and dry statistics are of little interest to anyone.

Once multiple crises strike simultaneously and their consequences begin to mount across different sectors, it is, of course, rather late to revisit someone's decisions or failures to act. This has only strengthened my desire to bring my professional experience back to my home county, not as an outside adviser, but by working on the ground alongside those who live in Ida-Viru County every day.

Over the past few years, I have found many dedicated, like-minded people in Ida-Viru County whose eyes still shine with trust, whose hearts are in the right place and who are firmly in tune with Estonia. I believe there are many more of them.

Ida-Viru is a process

We tend to talk about Ida-Viru County as a border region, industrial, Russian-speaking and shrinking. What else? The list could go on indefinitely, with a statistical table or deeply entrenched stereotype to back up every item. But this describes the current situation, not the direction in which the region is heading. And there is a consequence: When our region is consistently described in terms of its shortcomings, it is offered temporary relief measures rather than long-term investment.

The list of shortcomings can be extended endlessly. Perhaps now is the time to recognize the progress that has been made. Anyone who has lived, worked or regularly visited Ida-Viru County over the past two decades can see and knows just how much has changed. They can actually feel it because the transformation is not just about infrastructure, although that has changed, too. The biggest change is in the people.

Ida-Viru County is a region that has undergone restructuring across several industries within a single generation and the effects will continue to be felt. At the same time, studies conducted in the region reveal findings that challenge the widespread myth of local passivity: Helping neighbors and providing informal mutual support are part of everyday life in Ida-Viru County. People help one another without anyone having to organize them.

What is lacking is neither willingness nor compassion, but safe, welcoming meeting places that people feel are their own, along with trusted channels through which that willingness can translate into decisions. This is a very different diagnosis from passivity and therefore calls for a very different remedy.

Rethinking how we perceive Ida-Viru County is the first and least expensive thing we can do. Ida-Viru County offers a diverse range of resources for building the future: people, industry, skills, culture, nature and experience in navigating major upheavals. Few regions in Estonia have more experience of this kind. I believe that, under the right conditions, Ida-Viru County is capable of bringing renewed socioeconomic vitality not only to the region itself but to Estonia as a whole.

The "Ida-Viru Future 2050" program, launched as a civic initiative, has developed a vision for the region's future based on an extensive public engagement process involving public discussions, seminars, study visits, expert consultations and community workshops. The vision is grounded in the principle that sustainable development emerges when local people feel included in decision-making and believe their contributions matter.

The next decade is being decided now

There is a specific reason why the timing of this discussion matters. The national spatial plan "Estonia 2050" identifies the Ida-Viru urban area — Jõhvi, Kohtla-Järve, Narva and Sillamäe, which function together as a single regional center — as one of Estonia's three regional urban centers, alongside Tartu and Pärnu. The same document identifies it as a key area for Estonia's energy and economic transition. This is not a courtesy gesture, but the position of the Estonian state itself, set out in the country's foundational spatial development document through 2050.

Ida-Viru County is part of Estonia's eastern border region, a stretch of territory extending from the Gulf of Finland to Setomaa where the challenges are the same or very similar throughout: declining populations, disappearing services and stalled investment. The state's own analysis has concluded that this is a matter of national security and societal resilience.

This conclusion has practical implications. In regional policy, the usual question is where each euro invested will generate the greatest return. In national security, that question is asked far less often, although it should be. We do not maintain air surveillance and air defense systems because they are economically profitable, but because without them, the country would be blind and vulnerable. A depopulating border region that is losing hope poses the same kind of risk, only one that develops more slowly and is therefore politically easier to put off addressing.

These choices will come together in the national partnership agreement for 2028–2034. What does this mean for Ida-Viru County in practice? A child starting first grade in September 2028 will be in seventh grade by the time the agreement expires. Their entire school experience — the school building, extracurricular activities, swimming pool, bus routes, teachers' salaries and the next generation of teachers, their parent's or parents' jobs and opportunities for retraining or continuing education, the comfort and safety of public spaces and much more — will be shaped by decisions made over the next year and a half. The previous window of this kind opened in 2021. The next will not open until 2035.

Will the region come to the decision-making table with well-founded proposals or will it arrive largely through media coverage, bringing only its problems?

Pro-Estonian, European and successful

If I had to briefly describe what Ida-Viru County should look like in 2050, I would say it must be pro-Estonian, European and successful.

Being pro-Estonian means that the people who live here, regardless of the language they speak at home, feel a sense of ownership of our country rather than seeing themselves as temporary or permanent guests. Loyalty grows from the state's presence and from local people's genuine ability to make democratic decisions about their own lives.

Being European means building a normal European region where human rights are respected, public spaces are well maintained, public transportation works, services are accessible and businesses compete in the European market.

Being successful means that Ida-Viru County is a hub of socioeconomic activity — a place people come to live, study and work, rather than a place they leave. This is the most difficult of the three goals, but also the most measurable.

These three goals cannot be ranked or separated from one another. There is no point in constructing abstractions that have no personal relevance to anyone. I believe Ida-Viru County deserves the opportunity to foster a sense of belonging. Estonian, European, progressive. Three words, one idea.

So far, we have had varying degrees of success in strengthening pro-Estonian sentiment through language policy, education and culture. This work must continue.

The European dimension can be strengthened further and there is a concrete opportunity to do so: Narva's bid for the title of European Capital of Culture could become a shared undertaking for the entire region and the country. Progress is driven by both grassroots initiatives and major projects in business, urban planning and community life. Most importantly, people should experience the satisfaction of achieving success by making their home county a better place.

All of Estonia safer when things are in order in Ida-Viru County

Security is usually discussed in the context of the eastern border and the Russian-speaking population. This is appropriate, but somewhat incomplete. Societal resilience also depends on whether people trust their country enough to cooperate with it during a crisis. That kind of trust cannot be bought overnight. It is built over decades, not only through modern infrastructure or jobs, but through people's actual experience of having their local voices heard.

Every euro invested in developing employment and education, improving the living environment and strengthening communities in Ida-Viru County is also an investment in security, one that delivers returns even if no crisis ever occurs. When things are in order in Ida-Viru County, the whole of Estonia feels more secure. This works both ways and we know it.

The "Ida-Viru Future 2050" vision has now given rise to the Ida-Viru County Renewal Charter, which sets out concrete proposals on investment, housing, skills and services and community development. Each proposal comes with a measurable outcome to be achieved by the end of 2028. The charter, like the author of this opinion piece, is nonpartisan. It neither supports nor criticizes any political party and is addressed to all political forces and officials involved in preparing major development decisions.

No one claims this plan is perfect. But I would argue that a good plan for Ida-Viru County now is better than a perfect plan in the future. Ida-Viru County deserves more so that all of Estonia can enjoy better, safer and more prosperous lives. Ida-Viru County is not merely a recipient of prosperity; it is a co-creator and contributor because Estonia's prosperity grows when we build it together.

World.title: Argo Ideon: Our everyday doomscrolling
World.content:
The vigilant citizen begins their day by examining drone warnings and war maps. Estonia is living in a recurring cycle of war anxiety that social media abundantly feeds, writes Argo Ideon.

A security‑aware citizen wakes briskly, ahead of the alarm clock, as a jittery feeling is already there. They search for the smartphone under the blanket to check whether the Defense Forces have sent a drone warning. Today, there is no air threat, but if there is, then one must examine which area is being talked about. More precise instructions can be found at kriis.ee.

Since no dread‑inducing events occurred overnight, they may briefly wipe the sleepy eyes, but the vigilance cannot be lost. The information‑hungry citizen opens channel X. Yesterday, a map appeared there, where the Baltic states were depicted together with red arrows arriving from the east. Especially thick arrows were painted toward Narva and the Lithuania‑Poland border.

Now they would like to see whether the arrows moved somewhere further during sleep or stayed behind the eastern border. There, where according to retired General Martin Herem preparations may be underway "to do something militarily against us." But the new reports keep coming, the map has disappeared and whoever posted it at night is already forgotten about.

The citizen is confused, but realizes that instead of searching for the map they should visit the bathroom. On the way to get the toothbrush they glance out the kitchen window; against the background of drizzle everything seems even too calm, someone is walking their floppy‑eared dog on the sidewalk. An enemy agent, a saboteur recruited via social media? More likely the downstairs neighbor...

Turning on the shower, the citizen recalls that Estonia's defense expenditure budget next year is €2.2 billion. They set their fingers in pistol position and imitate a K9 Thunder self‑propelled howitzer shot: "Pow!" The wet environment does not hinder the Defense Forces' fire‑support capability.

And then there is HIMARS. The citizen does not know exactly what sound it makes, but they think that flying toward the target the much talked about weapon should sound something like a "Woosh!" As of today there have not been any new messages yet that the long‑ago ordered HIMARS ammunition from the U.S. is to definitely arrive in Estonia, already, soon.

A fresh interview with a national‑defense expert has appeared on the news portal. The situation is tense, the scenarios detailed and the threats hybrid. But it still is not a real war, and after reading the gut feeling remains that nothing new was learned. Therefore all the material must be worked through.

Let's begin with security expert Rainer Saks' every‑morning post. The citizen opens Facebook to see the original text, although several other websites also reprint Rainer's work. Rainer doesn't deal in nonsense — he says what he knows and how things are in Ukraine. Amazing how he has the stamina for this fifth year. Then the citizen opens the latest war diary in Eesti Ekspress. ERR's Ukraine blog constantly adds reports from early morning onward. Armed with up‑to‑date security information, the citizen dares to switch off war topics in their head for a while and focus on today's workday.

In the evening everything begins again from the start. On X there is a new set of maps with arrows. Putin is said to have said something about Estonia, but what exactly and in what context? And what does it actually mean? Are they fortifying the Narva River bank again? All of it seems extremely suspicious.

The worst anxiety takes hold again. Where's the box of pills?

Finally, the vigilant citizen remembers Robert Sheckley's classic sci‑fi horror story "Ghost V": "You can't beat blankets over the head for protection."

It should help against the Grumbler, the Purple-Striped Grabber, and the fear stories that pour daily like a torrent from social media.

In their restless sleep the security‑interested citizen sees how they build together with Pooh and Piglet the Hundred Acre Defense Line. Pooh carries three empty honey jars in front of the bedroom door, but Piglet takes a large wooden spoon and stands guard beside the door.

World.title: Syria to provide alternative route for Iraq’s oil exports
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Syria is providing a path for Iraqi petroleum exports to circumvent the dangerous Strait of Hormuz, with a fleet of tanker trucks lining up to transport oil overland to Baniyas port on the Mediterranean Sea.

In an interview with Bloomberg News, Yousef Qiblawy, CEO of the state-owned Syrian Petroleum Co., said that the Iraqi government has urged Syria to assist with crude exports in addition to existing fuel oil shipments.

“I expect Iraqi oil exports via Syria by tanker trucks to begin as soon as possible, as the agreement between the two countries is nearly finalized,” Qiblawy stated.

“Hopefully, by mid-October, the first convoy of tanker trucks carrying Iraqi oil will arrive in Syria,” Qiblawy added.

The logistical strategy would strengthen Syria’s position as a safe transit point for oil shipments from Iraq, which were hampered by the regional conflict that began at the end of February, as well as supplies from neighboring producers.

Iraq already uses a fleet of tanker trucks to transport part of its fuel oil to Syria’s Mediterranean port of Baniyas, where it is loaded onto vessels to be sold to global markets.

Baghdad is aiming to boost its oil income after the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz severely affected its economy.

Additionally, Iraqi oil shipments started flowing to Jordan in early August through the Trebil border crossing, the only land border crossing between the two countries, at a rate of 10,000 barrels per day.

The Iraqi oil is stored in the facilities of the Jordan Oil Terminals Company (JOTC), Jordan’s state-owned petroleum logistics and independent storage provider, before it is shipped to customers.

Syrian Petroleum Co. intends to provide storage tanks for Iraqi oil near Baniyas, according to Qiblawy, who spoke on the sidelines of the Energy Intelligence Forum in London this week.

The quantities transported to Syria account for a minor percentage of Iraq’s total oil exports, which the government claimed averaged around 2.7 million barrels per day last month.

World.title: Iraq offers $2.80 per barrel discount for November oil sales
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s State Oil Marketing Organization (SOMO) has established the November official selling price for Basrah Medium crude oil to Asia, which is $2.80 per barrel, lower than the Oman/Dubai average.

This price fluctuation reflects a dynamic shifting strategy in Middle Eastern petroleum flows, fueled mostly by regional conflict concerns, rising transportation expenses, and fierce competition for market dominance.

The selling price for Basrah Medium crude to Asian consumers is set at a discount of $2.80 per barrel less than the benchmark for Oman and Dubai.

The development comes after a big historical reduction in October, when SOMO aggressively increased discounts for October shipments to between $34.50 and $37.00 per barrel below regional benchmarks to secure clients despite logistical constraints.

Iraq’s action follows a larger pattern of activity among Gulf producers. Earlier this week, Saudi Arabia suddenly reduced its November selling price for Arab Light crude to Asia by a $3 to $5 discount per barrel below the Oman/Dubai benchmark.

Iraq and other Gulf states are offering significant discounts to handle extraordinary geopolitical and physical obstacles.

Escalating regional instability, particularly interruptions in the Strait of Hormuz, has raised shipping costs and insurance prices.

Producers are heavily lowering the Free on Board (FOB) price to cover significant transportation expenses, ensuring that the final delivered price stays competitive for customers in Asia.

With increased US sanctions on Iranian imports, independent Chinese refiners have switched to sulfur-rich Iraqi oil as an alternative.

Major foreign trading companies, notably Vitol Group, Trafigura, and Mercuria, have taken steps to distribute Iraqi oil as SOMO implements structural flexibility to protect national oil earnings, which account for more than 85 percent of Iraq’s federal budget.

World.title: Iraqi Airways resumes flights to Iran
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Airways resumed flights between Najaf and Tehran on Thursday, with the first flight arriving in the Iranian capital after the airline obtained a US exemption allowing it to restart flights to Iran.

Iranian media reported that the Iraqi aircraft landed at Imam Khomeini International Airport (IKIA) at 7:30 a.m., marking the return of daily direct flights on the Najaf-Tehran route.

Iraqi Airways announced on Monday the resumption of direct flights to Iran starting October 8, as part of a plan to operate regular daily flights between Najaf International Airport and airports in Tehran, Mashhad, and Isfahan.

The Iraqi Ministry of Transport stated that the plan aims to facilitate passenger travel and provide regular air transport options between Iraq and Iranian cities.

The ministry revealed in late September that Iraq’s national carrier will resume flights to Iran in October, amid flight suspension due to US sanctions limiting services to Iranian airlines.

Iraq previously imposed a ban on flights to and from Iran to adhere to US sanctions. The Iraqi government sought exemptions for travel related to pilgrimage, medical treatment, and education.

According to a source in Iraq’s transport ministry, the US Treasury Department approved a one-month exception.

The US administration offered Iraqi Airways a one-month US Treasury waiver to fly between Iran and Najaf, with the possibility of a permanent exemption.

Baghdad offered to provide passenger screening and information exchange to prevent airplanes from transporting weapons, sanctioned individuals, or illegal funds.

World.title: Iraq’s oil revenues hit $5 billion per month
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The spokesperson for the Iraqi Oil Ministry, Salim al-Rikabi, said on Thursday that the country’s oil exports during October are stable at a level of 2.7 million barrels per day, with the majority shipped from the southern terminals via the Strait of Hormuz.

Al-Rikabi explained that financial revenues generated from oil exports and other products range between $4.5 billion and $5 billion monthly, bolstering the country’s general budget.

Iraq’s oil exports increased in October to around 2.7 million barrels per day; approximately 2.4 million barrels come from the southern region, while export volumes from the northern region—including crude from Iraqi Kurdistan oilfields—range between 250,000 and 300,000 barrels per day.

These quantities are maintained despite the present crisis and challenges associated with production cuts, according to al-Rikabi.

The Iraqi official stressed that maintaining these export levels represents a big success for the Ministry of Oil.

Iraq’s oil exports include not only crude oil but also various petroleum products, such as fuel oil. The revenue generated from these exports contributes to the country’s federal budget.

World.title: ISIS claims responsibility for attack on Iraqi police in Kirkuk
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – ISIS claimed responsibility on Tuesday for an attack targeting Iraqi police forces southwest of the city of Kirkuk, which killed one police officer and injured others.

The attack is the first against Iraqi security forces since the withdrawal of the US-led international coalition from Iraq on September 30, ending the US military mission in the country.

The United States had led an international coalition to support Iraqi forces in their war against the terrorist group, including efforts to prevent the militant organization from regrouping.

Washington announced that it would continue to provide limited training and intelligence support following the withdrawal, with Iraqi forces assuming full responsibility for the country’s security and the suppression of the terrorist group’s remnants.

Prior to the pullout, Iraqi security officials cautioned that the group still has sleeper cells across Iraq, despite its defeat and the collapse of its rule in 2017.

The U.S. withdrawal raised concerns about a potential security vacuum that could give ISIS an opportunity to regain its strength, as some officials warned that Iraqi forces would now be compelled to contain the organization without foreign military presence.

In 2014, the terrorist group ISIS took control of large areas in Iraq and Syria before being defeated in 2017.

Over five million Iraqis had to flee the governorates of Nineveh, Salah al-Din, parts of Kirkuk, Diyala, and Anbar because of ISIS control over these areas in 2014.

Although Iraq declared in late 2017 that all of its regions were free of ISIS, the government continues to conduct security operations to hunt out any remaining members of the terrorist group.

World.title: Stocks fall further as oil spike fans fresh inflation worries
World.content:
Hong Kong – Equities extended losses Thursday as inflation fears were stoked by a fresh jump in oil prices following a report that said Donald Trump was considering more Iran strikes ahead of next month’s US midterm elections.

The selling tracked a retreat on Wall Street, where tech firms pulled back from recent gains, having weathered concerns over spiking borrowing costs and geopolitical uncertainty.

Crude had started the week on the back foot thanks to signs that exports from the Middle East were heading back towards pre-war levels and that G7 nations had agreed to tap their stockpiles.

But anxiety returned as figures showed Tehran had increased strikes on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, Houthis rebutted claims they had lost key territory and top oil officials warned that global reserves were running worryingly low.

And on Wednesday, The Atlantic reported that the White House had asked the Pentagon to draw up options to hit sites in Iran ahead of the midterms, with Trump’s Republicans in danger of losing both houses of Congress.

The article said the size and targets were still being discussed, but added that a wider operation could be in the works after the polls on November 3.

It added that even its proponents did not think the attacks would bring Tehran to talks or see Hormuz reopened, but hoped they would show strength leading into the vote.

Both main crude contracts rose more than one percent Thursday, with supplies also hit by the loss of more than 500,000 barrels of Gulf of Mexico output owing to producers shutting up shop as Tropical Storm Isaias approaches.

News that International Energy Agency members were ready to tap more oil from reserves did little to assuage worried traders.

The spike in oil prices fanned inflation fears again and put fresh upward pressure on government bond yields to multi-year highs.

After all three main indexes on Wall Street dropped — with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq off records — Asia followed suit.

Tokyo, Hong Kong, Sydney, Singapore, Seoul, Wellington, Taipei and Manila were all well down, though Shanghai edged up as investors returned from a week-long break.

– Tech earnings –

US Federal Reserve officials expect to hike interest rates again before the end of the year, according to minutes of their September meeting, where everyone agreed to the first increase since July 2023.

“With regard to the outlook for monetary policy beyond the current meeting, most participants assessed that another increase in the target range for the federal funds rate would likely be appropriate by year end,” the minutes said.

Several participants said they viewed the previous policy rate as not being adequately restrictive of economic activity, while they saw signs of renewed strength in the economy.

Investors are also gearing up for earnings season, with tech firms in the spotlight as questions over their profitability and elevated valuations swirl in light of the vast sums they have pumped into the AI sector.

“The headline earnings numbers may still be very strong. But with expectations elevated, valuations demanding and Treasury yields near multi-decade highs, the investment hurdle has become higher as well,” warned Charu Chanana at Saxo Markets.

“This season should therefore be less about simply identifying who beat consensus by the largest amount,” she said.

“The stronger businesses may be those that can deliver growth above expectations, convert that growth into cash, fund future investment from a strong balance sheet and still offer enough earnings upside to justify their valuation.”

South Korean titan Samsung’s shares fell as it forecast a more than 780 percent leap in third-quarter operating profit — thanks to high memory chip prices — but missed expectations.

It estimated July-September profit of 107.4 trillion won ($80.3 billion), up 782.5 percent on-year, but analysts on average had tipped 108.7 trillion won.

On currency markets, the euro remains wedged at lows last seen in June last year following another heavy fall amid worries about France’s high debt levels, which have spooked bond markets.

World.title: Samsung expects 780% quarterly operating profit jump on AI boom
World.content:
Seoul – Samsung Electronics forecast Thursday a more than 780 percent leap in third-quarter operating profit from a year earlier, buoyed by high memory chip prices as AI fuels a global supply shortage.

The South Korean giant is the world’s largest maker of memory chips — components now in huge demand as advanced types are snapped up for use in data centres powering artificial intelligence.

It estimated July-September operating profit at 107.4 trillion won ($80.1 billion), up 782.5 percent on-year, according to a company statement.

That would mark the first time a South Korean company has surpassed 100 trillion won in quarterly operating profit.

Revenue likely rose 127 percent to 195 trillion won, Samsung said.

With both numbers hitting all-time highs, the company will have broken its own records for both sales and operating profit for four consecutive quarters.

Samsung is expected to release its final quarterly earnings report at the end of October.

The AI boom has already helped Samsung and other semiconductor giants around the world post record profits this year.

Analysts at South Korean brokerage Shinhan Securities have struck a bullish stance on Samsung’s trajectory, writing in a note last week that they expected to see “even stronger earnings” from the company next year.

“Samsung Electronics now appears all set for a rapid increase in market share,” they said, as the company ramps up production of a new generation of high-bandwidth memory (HBM) chips, called HBM4.

– Worker demands –

Samsung, its South Korean rival SK hynix and US giant Micron dominate the global market for HBM — advanced chips used in AI data centres alongside other powerful data-crunching semiconductors.

“The transition to next-generation HBM will open up the opportunity to renegotiate prices” for Samsung, “helping to guarantee solid margins,” the Shinhan Securities note said.

While Samsung’s earnings have surged on strong demand for the memory chips it produces, the boom has also pushed up prices for DRAM and NAND flash used in smartphones — forcing the company’s mobile division to pay more for the same chips.

Analysts say rising production costs have become increasingly difficult to absorb as Samsung seeks to limit price increases to maintain shipment volumes and market share.

In August, Samsung announced a buyback of up to $80 billion of its own stock to boost shareholder returns.

It said the shareholder return plan was designed to ensure that the “fruits of the company’s growth translate into tangible benefits” for shareholders.

As earnings skyrocket for chipmakers including Samsung, many workers are demanding a bigger cut of the profits.

Samsung averted a strike in South Korea earlier this year by agreeing to a deal to distribute bonuses equivalent to 10.5 percent of operating profit to its semiconductor employees.

The agreement means around 78,000 employees from Samsung’s 125,000-strong domestic workforce are eligible to receive a bonus of roughly $370,000 this year, based on a market estimate of profits.

But in Taiwan on Wednesday, union representatives said hundreds of workers at a Micron plant had voted in favour of a strike, after talks with the US company over bonus reforms collapsed.

World.title: Microsoft pushes AI vision with new, expensive Surface laptop
World.content:
San Francisco – Microsoft is pushing a “hybrid intelligence” future with a new Surface Ultra laptop that runs on Nvidia artificial intelligence (AI) chips and will cost more than $2,500, the company announced Wednesday.

The launch is part of a broader push by tech companies to release hardware that can handle more AI computing on-device and offline, so users don’t have to rely solely on remote cloud data centers, where running AI is slower and more expensive.

It also sees Nvidia, whose data center processors power the AI revolution, make a move into personal computing, a sector dominated for decades by chips from Intel and Qualcomm.

“The trajectory for me is so clear. There will never be a moment where we will go and look and say: ‘Oh, this runs locally, this runs in the cloud.’ You will expect this hybrid intelligence to be everywhere and pervasive,” CEO Satya Nadella said during an event in San Francisco.

He was joined onstage by Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who echoed the idea that AI will be integrated into all computing going forward and on all devices.

Agentic AI, in particular, will be central to software development, Huang said, referring to systems programmed to be autonomous and perform tasks without supervision.

With all the changes from AI, “the computer has to be revolutionized,” Huang said.

The partnership between the two US-based tech titans helps them compete with Apple, Intel and AMD in the personal computing market.

Apple unveiled two desktop computers in September, the Mac mini and Mac Studio, which it touted as powerful new options capable of processing AI software locally.

Microsoft has been working on building “AI PCs” since at least 2024, when its laptops were powered by Qualcomm chips.

The new Surface Ultra will use Nvidia’s state-of-the-art AI chip, RTX Spark, which the semiconductor giant announced earlier this year.

It will cost $2,599 and begins shipping on October 16.

Some AI computing power and data will be processed locally, or on the device, while other applications are still handled remotely via Microsoft’s cloud computing services.

“We built it for developers and creators pushing the limits of performance,” Microsoft Executive Vice President of Windows and Device Pavan Davuluri said on Wednesday.

The news comes just a couple of weeks after Microsoft announced it would integrate Word, Excel and Powerpoint into its AI-powered assistant Copilot, in an effort to make AI the entry point for its famous suite of productivity software.

OpenAI, the company behind ChatGPT, and Claude-maker Anthropic each launched their own document creation tools in recent months.

The two San Francisco-based AI labs are also key suppliers for Microsoft, since Copilot runs primarily on their models.

Microsoft’s in-house models currently only power a few products, such as GitHub’s Copilot coding tool.

In June, Microsoft also unveiled its own cutting-edge artificial intelligence models — a crucial step toward reducing its dependence on OpenAI, the creator of ChatGPT.

Microsoft, the first company to have invested massively in OpenAI, has for several years been seeking to reduce its reliance on its Sam Altman-led partner.

It renegotiated their alliance last year and retains only a non-exclusive license on its technology until 2032 though is OpenAI’s biggest shareholder.

World.title: KPSC scam candidates taken to resorts, provided with Q&A: ED
World.content:
Karnataka Public Service Commission recruitment process was manipulated through an organised mechanism to generate proceeds of crime, ED said

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Enforcement Directorate on Thursday claimed that in the Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC) paper leak case, candidates for the veterinary officers' exam were taken to resorts/Airbnb a day before the exam, provided test papers and their answer sheets, all for Rs 40 lakh per candidate.Two days ago, the agency had arrested KPSC ex-chairman Shivashankarappa and its member B V Geetha.Giving details of its investigation into alleged corruption in Karnataka PSC, the agency said Gyanendra Gangwar, the arrested IAS officer who was controller of examinations at KPSC, was in custody of confidential examination material and had leaked them to Geetha. The ED said an organised syndicate paid bribes to officials from top to bottom.The ED's probe by its Bengaluru unit is based on multiple FIRs registered by the police at Vidhana Soudha police station in the case of recruitment of 400 veterinary officers."Evidence gathered so far has revealed an organised mechanism for generation of proceeds of crime through manipulation of the KPSC recruitment process. KPSC officials leaked question papers and candidate specific answer keys," the ED added.ED searched the premises of former Shivashankarappa and Geetha on Oct 6, which was followed by their arrest."The searches resulted in seizure of blank signed cheques of Rs 80 lakh, along with blank signed promissory notes, from one of the successful candidates," the ED said. The agency has traced at least 10 successful candidates who were allegedly taken to a resort/Airbnb villa on the outskirts of Bengaluru a day before the examination, where they were provided with a question paper and correct answer options and made to practice/memorise them.According to the ED, the question paper (marked with correct answers) containing 80 questions was leaked by Gangwar through his close associate, Basavaraj Kannale, to these 10 candidates."Basavaraj Kannale has collected bribe money amounting to Rs 40-50 lakh from each candidate, in consideration of facilitating their final selection in the veterinary officers' recruitment exam," ED said.Gangwar and Kannale were arrested on Sept 17-18 and sent to ED custody for 14 days. "During ED custody, Gangwar disclosed crucial information relating to irregularities in conducting various KPSC recruitment exams," ED added.

World.title: Jharkhand should 'revisit' DGP appointment rules, says Supreme Court
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Thursday said the Jharkhand's DGP appointment process prima facie violated its Prakash Singh judgement, which mandated consideration of officers with six months or more residual tenure for the top police post, reports Dhananjay Mahapatra.

It issued a notice to Tadasha Singh, who was appointed to the post a day before her retirement.

On an application filed by Centre alleging the state's DGP appointment regulation overreached the court's judgement, a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said, "In the event of the regulation being annulled, the appointment of Tadasha Mishra... would be required to be set aside. Therefore, we deem it appropriate to accord her one opportunity of being heard, for which Jharkhand govt is directed to serve notice on her to enable her to appear.

World.title: IPS quota in CAPF posts comes into force
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Central Armed Police Forces (General Administration) Act, 2026 - which stipulates that 50% of the posts in CAPFs at the level of inspector general, a minimum of 67% of the posts at the level of additional director general, and 100% of the posts at the level of director general and special director general-level, be filled by IPS officers on deputation - came into force Thursday.

The home ministry, in a notification, specified Oct 8 as the "appointed day" on which the provisions of the Act would come into force.

The operationalisation of the IPS quota in senior CAPF posts comes days after Union home secretary Govind Mohan told Supreme Court that the deputation of 46 IPS officers across five paramilitary forces (CRPF, BSF, CISF, ITBP and SSB), since the court's May 2025 direction for a gradual reduction in the number of IPS officers on deputation within two years, was in accordance with the law since SC had not held that such deputation should be discontinued altogether.

World.title: AI use ups homework scores, but slashes exam marks: Study
World.content:
âLLM users show lower cognitive effortâ (representative image)

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Evidence cited by World Bank suggests that unrestricted use of generative AI can improve what students submit as part of classwork while weakening what they actually learn - a warning with implications for countries such as India.World Development Report 2026 devotes a section to 'Generative AI and the Erosion of Knowledge, Learning, and Human Skills', cautioning that tools such as ChatGPT can reduce the mental effort through which reasoning, writing and knowledge are built.Its strongest evidence comes from China. A study covering students in classes VII-XII found self-reported AI use rising from almost zero to around 80% between 2022 and 2025. Six months after its first use, homework scores improved 18% even as students spe-nt less time on assignments, while monthly in-class examination scores fell 20%. Students who had ever used AI also scored, on average, 5-7% lower in senior high-school and college entrance exams.The report cautioned that the study had not yet been peer-reviewed and reflected the early phase of AI adoption.Gaurav Nayyar, who led the World Bank team that prepared the report, said the evidence points to both opportunity and risk in education."If students outsource the learning process to AI, then... that will be a problem," he told TOI.He said the evidence so far appeared more encouraging when AI was used by teachers rather than directly by students, pointing to its use in personalising and customising instructions to suit different learners.Other research reviewed by World Bank points in the same direction. Participants using large language models for research displayed lower cognitive effort and weaker reasoning, while studies found mental effort declining even when output quality improved. Students given unrestricted AI access also performed worse later when the technology was withdrawn.The report warns that if students use AI to complete homework, the "productive struggle" central to learning can disappear, potentially weakening foundational skills in reasoning and writing.But it does not argue against AI in education. A synthesis of experiments across China, Ghana, Nigeria, Turkiye and US found that 30 sessions of AI-powered tutoring produced learning gains equivalent to at least 0.5 years of schooling, particularly when AI complemented teachers and included safeguards against shortcuts. "AI can augment human capabilities," the report said, "but it must not replace the processes through which more advanced skills are acquired. "

World.title: Group of 42 ex-judges defends SIR, slams opposition attack on Election Commission
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A group of 42 retired judges on Thursday slammed the opposition's attack on

, claiming that it appeared to be a calculated campaign driven by "vested political interests" with little regard for the potentially devastating consequences of destabilising the world's largest democracy.

"India's constitutional bodies are under sustained attack. EC stands at the centre of this assault. Even the higher judiciary, which we hold in high esteem, and statutory agencies have not been spared. These attacks are not reasoned critique," they said in an open letter.

Former Supreme Court judges Hemant Gupta and Pankaj Mittal and several former chief justices of high courts, besides retired judges of various HCs were signatories to the statement, which defended the EC's Special Intensive Review (SIR) of electoral rolls, arguing that a clean roll protected every genuine vote.

They said they held no brief for any political party but in moments like these, silence was no longer a neutral choice. Constitutional authorities were now branded "thieves", "puppets" and "compromised" from public platforms, they said in a reference to EC's sharp criticism by opposition functionaries and organisations like CJP.

Targeting Congress, they said: "EVMs are blamed only after defeat. Victories won on the same machines go unquestioned.





A party that governed this nation for over five decades now claims that the very system which elected it is rigged."

They said activist outfits with a long record of selective litigation lent these claims a veneer of legality. "They file petitions one after the other. They seldom file proof. The courtroom becomes a stage, and when the judgement is delivered, it is criticised whenever it does not serve their interests."

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The uproar over SIR appeared both sudden and remarkably convenient, the judges said. "Tell citizens often enough that their vote does not count, and they stop believing in the ballot. When the ballot loses meaning, the street gains it. Unrest begins with a narrative. Anarchic and fringe elements then occupy the vacuum," the group said.

While some of these groups were homegrown, some took their cues from beyond borders, they alleged. They appealed to political parties to not delegitimise elections and take their grievances to EC and the courts with evidence.

NEW DELHI: Amid a rapid absorption of mobile phones and technology PM Narendra Modi called for a global effort to tackle cyber frauds and deepfakes, while asserting that phones were no longer communication devices but a powerful tool of governance.Addressing the India Mobile Congress, the PM said his govt had leveraged technology and connectivity for direct benefit transfer of Rs 50 lakh crore, which helped plug leakages of nearly Rs 5 lakh crore. Now, the "telecom revolution", he said, is driving service delivery, content, including in local languages, and gaming, but it came with challenges."At a time when telecom and digital technology are playing such a critical role, it is equally important that we strengthen the security framework associated with them," PM said, while urging govts, technology companies, telecom operators, and financial institutions to work together."I urge GSMA and telecom operators to come together and create a global mechanism to stop frauds even before they reach people. India has learned a great deal through its own experiences, and is ready to share the same with the world."Modi said the telecom boom was driven by a well-crafted policy framework, which sought to untangle the sector and also reduce AGR and other liabilities.

World.title: 4 FIRs against Rahul, Priyanka over anti-CEC protests in Delhi
World.content:
The protests continued for a third consecutive day on Thursday

NEW DELHI: The Delhi Police has so far registered at least four FIRs against Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and other opposition leaders in connection with the two-day protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar in Lutyens' Delhi, sources told news agency PTI on Thursday.The FIRs were registered under sections relating to assault, obstructing public servants from discharging their duties and violation of Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), the sources told PTI. The development came a day after police registered an FIR against Rahul and Priyanka for allegedly forcing their way into Akashvani Bhawan. Police had detained 91 people, including several MPs, during Wednesday's protest.The opposition leaders had been stopped while attempting to march to Jantar Mantar for a sit-in demanding Kumar's resignation over allegations of "vote chori". Rahul Gandhi had earlier claimed that around 300 MPs wanted to hold a peaceful protest but were stopped by police and "beaten up".The protests continued for a third consecutive day on Thursday, with INDIA bloc leaders staging a sit-in at Mahatma Gandhi's memorial at Rajghat.The opposition has accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Home Minister Amit Shah and CEC Kumar of "hijacking" the country through an alleged conspiracy involving "vote chori".Rahul Gandhi said Modi, Shah, RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat and Kumar had "destroyed the Constitution and stolen votes", asserting that they would be brought to justice."The truth is that Narendra Modi, Amit Shah, Mohan Bhagwat, and Gyanesh Kumar have hijacked the country through a criminal conspiracy. They have destroyed the Constitution and stolen votes," he said.Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said the opposition had come to Rajghat to pray for "wisdom" for the government and the Election Commission, while demanding that alleged irregularities in the electoral process be stopped.The opposition leaders are also seeking time to meet President Droupadi Murmu to present their case and demand Kumar's dismissal.Congress leaders and representatives of the CPI-M, CPI, TMC, RJD and SP said the agitation would continue on Friday.
